citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): [Vinyl chloride (PVC) manufacturing: Liver angiosarcoma; Asbestos mining, construction work, shipbuilding (asbestos): Lung cancer and mesothelioma]

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: How do cancer cells utilize 'aerobic glycolysis' to support development?
back: They reprogram glucose metabolism (Warburg effect) to generate intermediates for biosynthetic pathways (nucleosides/amino acids) needed for new cells.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): [increased production of glycolytic intermediates can be fed into various biosynthetic pathways, including those that generate the nucleosides and amino acids, necessary for the production of new cells.]

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: List three specific malignancies linked to UV radiation exposure.
back: 1. Basal cell carcinoma. 2. Melanoma. 3. Non-melanocytic skin cancer.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): [UV exposure: Basal cell carcinoma, Melanoma, Non-melanocytic skin cancer]

category: Identify the risk factors for cancer development
front: Which lifestyle factor is responsible for >20% of global cancer deaths and 80% of male lung cancer?
back: Cigarette smoking.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 158 (Book Page): Cigarette smoking accounts for more than 20% of all global cancer deaths, 80% of lung cancer cases in men.

category: Identify the risk factors for cancer development
front: How does a mutation in the TP53 'guardian of the genome' gene promote cancer development?
back:
1. Impairs induction of apoptosis in response to DNA damage.
2. Allows accumulation of driver genomic aberrations.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 158 (Book Page): The most important regulator of apoptosis is the TP53 tumour suppressor gene... Disruption... leads to the accumulation of driver genomic aberrations.

category: Identify the risk factors for cancer development
front: Contrast the prevalence of inherited cancer syndromes with multifactorial environmental cancers.
back:
1. Inherited syndromes: 5–10% of all cancers.
2. Majority: Result from complex interactions between genetic factors and environmental carcinogens.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): The majority of cancers... result of a complex interaction between genetic factors and exposure to environmental carcinogens... inherited cancer syndromes... account for 5%–10%.

category: Identify the risk factors for cancer development
front: Identify the specific cancer risks associated with occupational asbestos exposure in construction or shipbuilding.
back:
1. Lung cancer.
2. Mesothelioma.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Asbestos mining, construction work, shipbuilding (asbestos) [leads to] Lung cancer and mesothelioma.

category: Identify the risk factors for cancer development
front: Identify the medical risk factor for developing acute myeloid leukaemia (AML) in a cancer survivor.
back: Previous treatment with cytotoxic chemotherapy (e.g., alkylating agents or topoisomerase II inhibitors).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 176 (Book Page): Secondary acute leukaemia (mostly AML) can occur 1–2 years after treatment with topoisomerase II inhibitors, or 2–5 years after treatment with alkylating agents.

category: Identify the risk factors for cancer development
front: List three high-risk infectious agents and their specifically associated primary cancer sites.
back:
1. HPV: Cervical/Anal cancer.
2. H. pylori: Gastric cancer.
3. HBV/HCV: Hepatocellular carcinoma.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Viral infection: HPV (Cervical), HBV and HCV (Hepatocellular); Bacterial: H. pylori (Gastric).

category: Identify the risk factors for cancer development
front: Which specific dietary intakes are established risk factors for colonic and gastric cancers?
back:
1. Low-roughage/high-fat content diet (Colon).
2. High nitrosamine intake (Gastric).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Low-roughage/high-fat content diet (Colonic cancer); High nitrosamine intake (Gastric cancer).

category: Identify the risk factors for cancer development
front: Identify the inheritance pattern and associated gene for Li-Fraumeni syndrome.
back:
1. Inheritance: Autosomal Dominant (AD).
2. Gene: TP53.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 163 (Book Page): Li–Fraumeni syndrome... AD... TP53.

category: Identify the risk factors for cancer development
front: By what physiological mechanism does obesity increase the risk of endometrial and breast cancers?
back: Increased oestrogen levels (and reduced physical activity).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Obesity [leads to] Increased oestrogen [predisposing to] Breast and endometrial cancer.

category: Identify the risk factors for cancer development
front: What is the primary environmental cause of carcinomas of the cervix worldwide?
back: Infection with Human Papillomavirus (HPV), specifically high-risk subtypes 16 and 18.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): ...most carcinomas of the cervix are related to infection with human papillomavirus (HPV subtypes 16 and 18).

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: What is the most significant preventable environmental risk factor for global cancer mortality?
back:
Cigarette smoking: 
- Accounts for >20% of all global cancer deaths.
- Causes 80% of lung cancer in men and 50% in women.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 158 (Book Page): [Cigarette smoking accounts for more than 20% of all global cancer deaths, 80% of lung cancer cases in men and 50% of lung cancer cases in women worldwide]

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: How does the TP53 gene mutation contribute to the 'resisting cell death' hallmark?
back:
Loss of 'guardian of genome' function: 
- Normally induces apoptosis via DNA damage sensing.
- Mutation prevents disassembly of damaged cells, enabling survival of genomic aberrations.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 160 (Book Page): [The most important regulator of apoptosis is the TP53 tumour suppressor gene, often described as the ‘guardian of the genome’... Disruption of p53 protein function... are found in over half of cancers.]

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: Contrast the genetic basis of Lynch Syndrome (HNPCC) versus Familial Adenomatous Polyposis (FAP).
back:
Lynch Syndrome: Mismatch repair gene mutations (MSH2, MLH1, MSH6).
FAP: Mutation in the APC gene (adenomatous polyposis coli).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 163 (Book Page): [Familial adenomatous polyposis: APC gene; Hereditary non-polyposis colon cancer (HNPCC): MSH2, MLH1, MSH6]

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: A 25-year-old with breast cancer and family history of sarcomas likely has which genetic syndrome?
back:
Li-Fraumeni syndrome:
- Caused by inherited TP53 mutation.
- Predisposes to early-onset breast cancer, sarcomas, brain tumors, and leukemias.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 163 (Book Page): [Li–Fraumeni syndrome: Malignancies: Sarcoma, breast, osteosarcoma, leukaemia, glioma; Gene: TP53]

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: Which targeted therapy step utilizes the 'synthetic lethality' principle in BRCA-mutated cancers?
back:
PARP inhibition:
- Exploits defective DNA repair in BRCA-mutated cells.
- Examples: Olaparib, Niraparib used in ovarian/breast cancer management.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 150 (Book Page): [Options include... targeted therapy against poly-ADP ribose polymerase (PARP, e.g. olaparib, niraparib or rucaparib).]

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: List the specific infectious environmental agents for Cervical and Nasopharyngeal cancers.
back:
- Cervical Cancer: Human Papillomavirus (HPV) subtypes 16 and 18.
- Nasopharyngeal Cancer: Epstein–Barr virus (EBV).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): [Viral infection: Epstein–Barr virus (Nasopharyngeal cancer); Human papillomavirus (Cervical cancer)]

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: What molecular transition allows cancer cells to initiate the 'Invasion-Metastasis Cascade'?
back:
Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition (EMT):
- Loss of E-cadherin (cell-cell adhesion molecule).
- Enables cells to break through the basement membrane and enter bloodstream (intravasation).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 160 (Book Page): [The initiation of this process is enabled by epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT)... Cancer cells... lose normal cell–cell adhesion through the down-regulation... of E-cadherin]

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: Differentiate the primary cancer risk for a worker in the dye industry versus an asbestos miner.
back:
- Dye/Rubber Industry: Bladder cancer (due to aromatic amines).
- Asbestos Exposure: Lung cancer and Mesothelioma.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): [Dye and rubber manufacturing (aromatic amines): Bladder cancer; Asbestos mining (asbestos): Lung cancer and mesothelioma]

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: Define 'Aerobic Glycolysis' (Warburg Effect) in cancer cellular energetics.
back:
Reprogramming metabolism to utilize glycolysis even in oxygen presence.
- Increases glycolytic intermediates for biosynthetic pathways (nucleosides/amino acids).
- Driven by up-regulation of GLUT1 transporters.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): [Cancer cells can reprogram their glucose metabolism to limit energy production to glycolysis, even in the presence of oxygen. This has been termed ‘aerobic glycolysis’.]

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: What proportion of cancers are strictly attributable to inherited cancer syndromes?
back:
5% to 10% of all cancers.
- Result from inherited mutations in driver genes (growth/death regulation).
- Often characterized by incomplete penetrance.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): [A number of inherited cancer syndromes are recognised and account for 5%–10% of all cancers.]

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
coreConcept: Impact of Smoking on Cancer Mortality
front: Q: What percentage of global cancer deaths is attributed to cigarette smoking?
back:
- More than 20% of all global cancer deaths.
- 80% of lung cancer cases in men.
- 50% of lung cancer cases in women.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 158 (Book Page): Cigarette smoking accounts for more than 20% of all global cancer deaths, 80% of lung cancer cases in men and 50% of lung cancer cases in women worldwide

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: What is the primary determinant in the development of the majority of cancers?
back:
- Complex interaction between genetic factors and exposure to environmental carcinogens.
- Most solid cancers demonstrate multifactorial pathogenesis.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): The majority of cancers do not have a single cause but rather are the result of a complex interaction between genetic factors and exposure to environmental carcinogens.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: What proportion of all cancers are accounted for by inherited cancer syndromes?
back:
- 5% to 10% of all cancers.
- Result from inherited mutations in driver genes regulating growth, death, and apoptosis.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): A number of inherited cancer syndromes are recognised and account for 5%–10% of all cancers.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: A woman carries a BRCA1 mutation. What clinical management options are available for prevention?
back:
- Regular screening investigations for early detection.
- Preventative treatments like prophylactic mastectomy.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): Patients and their family members may also benefit from screening investigations to detect cancer early, or preventative treatments such as prophylactic mastectomy in women who carry a BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: Match these chemicals to their specific cancers: Vinyl chloride and Benzene.
back:
- Vinyl chloride: Liver angiosarcoma.
- Benzene: Acute leukaemia.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Vinyl chloride (PVC) manufacturing: Liver angiosarcoma; Petroleum industry (benzene): Acute leukaemia.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: Name three specific infectious agents and the cancers they predispose to globally.
back:
- HPV (Types 16/18): Cervical/Anal cancer.
- Helicobacter pylori: Gastric cancer/MALT lymphoma.
- HBV/HCV: Hepatocellular carcinoma.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Human papillomavirus: Cervical cancer; Helicobacter pylori: Gastric cancer; Hepatitis B and C viruses: Hepatocellular carcinoma.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: Which dietary and lifestyle modifications are recommended to reduce cancer risk?
back:
- Avoid animal fat and red meat.
- Increase fiber, fresh fruit, and vegetable intake.
- Avoid obesity and increase physical activity.
- Reduce alcohol intake.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 158 (Book Page): Lifestyle modification could reduce these if steps were taken to avoid animal fat and red meat, reduce alcohol, increase fibre, fresh fruit and vegetable intake, avoid obesity and increase physical activity.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: A patient presents with multiple sarcomas and breast cancer. Which syndrome and gene are likely involved?
back:
- Li–Fraumeni syndrome.
- Gene: TP53 (Autosomal Dominant).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 163 (Book Page): Li–Fraumeni syndrome: Sarcoma, breast... Gene: TP53

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: How does obesity contribute to the development of breast and endometrial cancers?
back:
- Chronic inflammatory state.
- Increased levels of circulating oestrogen.
- Reduced physical activity and increased insulin.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Obesity: Increased oestrogen... Breast and endometrial cancer.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: Which environmental toxin found in contaminated food supplies is a major cause of Hepatocellular Carcinoma?
back:
- Aflatoxin.
- Source: Aspergillus flavus (found in contaminated crops).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): The association between aflatoxin production within contaminated food supplies and hepatocellular carcinomas.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: What is the single most significant preventable environmental cause of cancer deaths globally?
back: Cigarette smoking; it accounts for over 20% of all global cancer deaths and 80% of lung cancer cases in men.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 158 (Book Page): [Cigarette smoking accounts for more than 20% of all global cancer deaths, 80% of lung cancer cases in men and 50% of lung cancer cases in women worldwide.]

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Explain the role of the TP53 gene in maintaining genomic integrity.
back: Known as the 'guardian of the genome,' it induces apoptosis or senescence in response to DNA damage; mutations exist in over 50% of cancers.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 158 (Book Page): [The most important regulator of apoptosis is the TP53 tumour suppressor gene, often described as the ‘guardian of the genome’... Disruption of p53 protein function as a result of mutations in the TP53 gene are found in over half of cancers.]

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Contrast the prevalence of inherited cancer syndromes with environmental/lifestyle-related cancers.
back: Inherited syndromes: 5%–10% of cases. Environmental/Lifestyle (diet, smoking, alcohol): Contributes to over 50% of the global cancer burden.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 158 (Book Page), 161: [Cigarette smoking accounts for more than 20%... Diet and alcohol contribute to a further 30%... A number of inherited cancer syndromes are recognised and account for 5%–10% of all cancers.]

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Which genetic mutations should be suspected in a young woman with a family history of breast and ovarian cancer?
back: BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutations; inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern; significantly increases risk for breast, ovarian, prostate, and pancreatic cancers.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 163 (Book Page): [Syndrome: Breast/ovarian; Malignancies: Breast, ovarian, colonic, prostatic, pancreatic; Inheritance: AD; Gene: BRCA1, BRCA2]

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: How does the 'Aerobic Glycolysis' (Warburg Effect) metabolic loop benefit cancer cell development?
back: Cancer cells reprogram glucose metabolism toward glycolysis even with oxygen; this provides biosynthetic intermediates (nucleosides, amino acids) for rapid cell division.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): [Cancer cells can reprogram their glucose metabolism to limit energy production to glycolysis, even in the presence of oxygen... increased production of glycolytic intermediates can be fed into various biosynthetic pathways... necessary for the production of new cells.]

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: List the four primary infectious agents that account for 15% of cancers worldwide.
back:
1. Human Papillomavirus (HPV).
2. Helicobacter pylori.
3. Hepatitis B and C viruses.
4. Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): [Viral infection: Epstein–Barr virus, Human papillomavirus, Hepatitis B and C viruses... Bacterial infection: Helicobacter pylori]

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: What is the mechanism by which Telomerase enables the hallmark of replicative immortality?
back: It adds nucleotides to telomeres, preventing the progressive shortening (mitotic clock) that normally triggers senescence or death in dividing cells.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 159 (Book Page): [Telomerase, a specialised polymerase enzyme, adds nucleotides to telomeres, allowing continued cell division and thus preventing premature arrest of cellular replication.]

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Differentiate Li-Fraumeni syndrome from Hereditary Non-Polyposis Colon Cancer (HNPCC) based on gene mutation.
back: Li-Fraumeni: TP53 mutation (Sarcomas/Breast). HNPCC: Mismatch repair genes (MSH2, MLH1, MSH6, etc.), leading to colonic and endometrial cancers.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 163 (Book Page): [Li–Fraumeni syndrome... TP53... Hereditary non-polyposis colon cancer (HNPCC)... MSH2, MLH1, MSH6, PMS1, PMS2]

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Which genetic marker in lung cancer dictates the clinical use of EGFR inhibitors like gefitinib?
back: Presence of activating EGFR mutations; found in approximately 15% of lung adenocarcinomas, predicting a positive response to targeted therapy.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 175 (Book Page): [Approximately 15% of lung adenocarcinomas have activating mutations of EGFR, which may be targeted with drugs such as gefitinib, erlotinib or osimertinib.]

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Identify the environmental carcinogen linked to Aspergillus flavus and its associated malignancy.
back: Carcinogen: Aflatoxin. Malignancy: Hepatocellular Carcinoma (HCC).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page)-162: [the association between aflatoxin production within contaminated food supplies and hepatocellular carcinomas... Aflatoxin from contamination of Aspergillus flavus: Hepatocellular cancer]

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: What percentage of all cancers are attributed to inherited cancer syndromes?
back: 5%–10% of all cancers.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): A number of inherited cancer syndromes are recognised and account for 5%–10% of all cancers.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: What is the primary environmental cause of cancer worldwide and its mortality impact?
back: Cigarette smoking; accounts for more than 20% of all global cancer deaths.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 158 (Book Page): Cigarette smoking accounts for more than 20% of all global cancer deaths.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: Contrast the cancer types associated with Human Papillomavirus (HPV) versus Helicobacter pylori.
back:
• HPV: Cervical, anal, and oropharyngeal cancer.
• H. pylori: Gastric MALT lymphomas and gastric cancer.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Box 7.1: Human papillomavirus (Cervical, anal, oropharyngeal cancer); Helicobacter pylori (Gastric MALT lymphomas, gastric cancer).

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: A patient with BRCA1 mutation seeks prevention. What surgical option is suggested?
back: Prophylactic mastectomy.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): Patients and their family members may also benefit from... preventative treatments such as prophylactic mastectomy in women who carry a BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: Which occupational exposure is specifically linked to liver angiosarcoma?
back: Vinyl chloride (PVC) manufacturing.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Box 7.1: Vinyl chloride (PVC) manufacturing: Liver angiosarcoma.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: In inherited syndromes, mutations typically affect which group of regulatory genes?
back: Driver genes regulating cell growth, cell death, and apoptosis.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): they result from inherited mutations in driver genes that regulate cell growth, cell death and apoptosis.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: List four lifestyle modifications to reduce the 30% of cancers linked to diet/alcohol.
back:
• Avoid red meat/animal fat.
• Reduce alcohol.
• Increase fiber/fruit/vegetables.
• Avoid obesity/increase physical activity.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 158 (Book Page): Lifestyle modification could reduce these if steps were taken to avoid animal fat and red meat, reduce alcohol, increase fibre, fresh fruit and vegetable intake, avoid obesity and increase physical activity.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: Differentiate cancer risks of UV exposure versus nuclear fallout radiation.
back:
• UV: Basal cell carcinoma, Melanoma.
• Nuclear fallout: Leukaemia and solid tumours (e.g., thyroid).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Box 7.1: UV exposure (Basal cell carcinoma, Melanoma); Nuclear fallout (Leukaemia, Solid tumours, e.g. thyroid).

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: Explain the link between Aflatoxin and hepatocellular carcinoma.
back: Aflatoxin produced by Aspergillus flavus in contaminated food supplies triggers the malignancy.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): the association between aflatoxin production within contaminated food supplies and hepatocellular carcinomas.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: What is the significance of rising breast cancer risk in Far Eastern migrants to the West?
back: Indicates environmental components (Western lifestyle/diet) override ethnicity in subsequent generations.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): The risk of breast cancer in women of Far Eastern origin... rises in subsequent generations to approach that of the resident population of the host country.

category: Identify the risk factors for cancer development
front: Q: What percentage of global cancer deaths is attributed to cigarette smoking?
back: More than 20% of all global cancer deaths (including 80% of lung cancers in men and 50% in women).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 158 (Book Page): [Cigarette smoking accounts for more than 20% of all global cancer deaths, 80% of lung cancer cases in men and 50% of lung cancer cases in women worldwide]

category: Identify the risk factors for cancer development
front: Q: How does a Western lifestyle modify breast cancer risk in migrants from the Far East?
back: Risk rises in subsequent generations due to higher saturated fat/dairy intake, later first pregnancy, and shifts in diurnal rhythms.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): [The precise environmental factors that cause this change are unclear but may include diet (higher intake of saturated fat and/or dairy products), reproductive patterns (later onset of first pregnancy) and lifestyle (increased use of artificial light and shift in diurnal rhythm).]

category: Identify the risk factors for cancer development
front: Q: Contrast the malignancies associated with Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV) versus Human Papillomavirus (HPV).
back: 1. EBV: Burkitt lymphoma and nasopharyngeal cancer. 2. HPV: Cervical, anal, and oropharyngeal cancers.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): [Box 7.1 Viral infection: Epstein-Barr virus (Burkitt lymphoma and nasopharyngeal cancer); Human papillomavirus (Cervical cancer, anal cancer, oropharyngeal cancer)]

category: Identify the risk factors for cancer development
front: Q: A patient working in PVC manufacturing presents with liver angiosarcoma. What is the likely risk factor?
back: Vinyl chloride exposure (specifically linked to the production of polyvinyl chloride).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): [Box 7.1 Vinyl chloride (PVC) manufacturing: Liver angiosarcoma]

category: Identify the risk factors for cancer development
front: Q: How does the latency of secondary AML differ between topoisomerase II inhibitors and alkylating agents?
back: 1. Topoisomerase II inhibitors: 1-2 years post-treatment. 2. Alkylating agents: 2-5 years post-treatment.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 176 (Book Page): [Secondary acute leukaemia (mostly AML) can occur 1-2 years after treatment with topoisomerase II inhibitors, or 2-5 years after treatment with alkylating agents.]

category: Identify the risk factors for cancer development
front: Q: What percentage of cancers are attributed to inherited cancer syndromes?
back: 5% to 10% of all cancers (resulting from inherited mutations in driver genes).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): [A number of inherited cancer syndromes are recognised and account for 5%-10% of all cancers.]

category: Identify the risk factors for cancer development
front: Q: Apply the multifactorial pathogenesis model to explain why diet and alcohol are significant cancer risk factors.
back: They contribute to 30% of cancers (stomach, colon, oesophagus, breast, liver) primarily through animal fat, red meat, and low fiber.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 158 (Book Page): [Diet and alcohol contribute to a further 30% of cancers, including those of the stomach, colon, oesophagus, breast and liver.]

category: Identify the risk factors for cancer development
front: Q: Differentiate the primary malignancies caused by UV radiation versus ionizing radiation (nuclear fallout).
back: 1. UV: Basal cell carcinoma and Melanoma. 2. Ionizing: Leukaemia and solid tumors (e.g., thyroid).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): [Box 7.1 UV exposure: Basal cell carcinoma, Melanoma; Nuclear fallout: Leukaemia, Solid tumours, e.g. thyroid]

category: Identify the risk factors for cancer development
front: Q: Explain the physiological link between obesity and the development of endometrial cancer.
back: Obesity leads to increased oestrogen levels, which increases the duration of unopposed oestrogen exposure.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 178 (Book Page): [Endometrial cancer is 10 times more common in obese women and this is thought to be due to elevated levels of oestrogens.]

category: Identify the risk factors for cancer development
front: Q: Which specific dietary contaminant is the primary risk factor for hepatocellular carcinoma?
back: Aflatoxin (produced by Aspergillus flavus contamination of food supplies).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): [the association between aflatoxin production within contaminated food supplies and hepatocellular carcinomas.]

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
coreConcept: Impact of Smoking on Global Cancer Mortality
front: What percentage of global cancer deaths is attributed to cigarette smoking?
back: More than 20% of all global cancer deaths (80% of lung cancer in men and 50% in women).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 158 (Book Page): Cigarette smoking accounts for more than 20% of all global cancer deaths, 80% of lung cancer cases in men and 50% of lung cancer cases in women worldwide.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Define the concept of 'Multistep Carcinogenesis' regarding genetic determinants.
back: Successive clonal expansions of pre-malignant cells triggered by the acquisition of random driver genomic aberrations.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 158 (Book Page): Multistep carcinogenesis results from successive clonal expansions of pre-malignant cells, each expansion being triggered by acquisition of a random driver aberration.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
coreConcept: Environmental vs. Genetic Influence on Cancer
front: Explain the significance of breast cancer risk in Far Eastern migrants to Western countries.
back: Highlights environmental dominance; risk rises in subsequent generations as they adopt Western diets (high saturated fat) and reproductive patterns.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): the risk of breast cancer in women of Far Eastern origin remains relatively low when they first migrate... but rises in subsequent generations to approach that of the resident population... factors... include diet... reproductive patterns.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: A patient is identified as a BRCA1 carrier. What are the recommended preventative clinical steps?
back:
1. Screening investigations (early detection)
2. Preventative treatments (e.g., prophylactic mastectomy)
3. Tailored anti-cancer therapy decisions.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): Patients and their family members may also benefit from screening investigations to detect cancer early, or preventative treatments such as prophylactic mastectomy in women who carry a BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Identify the specific occupational exposure linked to Liver Angiosarcoma.
back: Vinyl chloride (PVC) manufacturing.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Vinyl chloride (PVC) manufacturing - Liver angiosarcoma.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: What environmental factor is specifically associated with Gastric MALT lymphomas?
back: Bacterial infection with Helicobacter pylori.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Bacterial infection - Helicobacter pylori - Gastric MALT lymphomas, gastric cancer.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Define the role of 'Driver mutations' in the genetic evolution of a tumor.
back: Random genomic aberrations that confer a selective survival advantage, enabling overgrowth and dominance in local tissues.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 158 (Book Page): Rarely, aberrations will confer a selective survival advantage on single cells, ‘driving’ overgrowth and dominance in local tissue environments.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Which dietary contaminant is a principal environmental cause of hepatocellular carcinoma?
back: Aflatoxin produced by Aspergillus flavus in contaminated food supplies.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): the association between aflatoxin production within contaminated food supplies and hepatocellular carcinomas.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Contrast the metabolic pathways used by normal vs. cancer cells for energy production.
back:
Normal: Oxidative phosphorylation (aerobic).
Cancer: Aerobic glycolysis (Warburg effect), favoring glycolytic intermediates for biosynthesis despite lower ATP yield.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 133 (Book Page): Cancer cells can reprogram their glucose metabolism to limit energy production to glycolysis, even in the presence of oxygen. This has been termed ‘aerobic glycolysis’.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: What percentage of all cancers is accounted for by inherited cancer syndromes?
back: 5%–10% of all cancers.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): A number of inherited cancer syndromes are recognised and account for 5%–10% of all cancers.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: What percentage of global cancer deaths is directly attributed to cigarette smoking?
back: Over 20% of global cancer deaths (80% of lung cancer in men and 50% in women).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 158 (Book Page): Cigarette smoking accounts for more than 20% of all global cancer deaths, 80% of lung cancer cases in men and 50% of lung cancer cases in women worldwide.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: How does the TP53 gene function as the 'guardian of the genome'?
back: It induces apoptosis in response to significant genomic damage; mutations occur in over 50% of cancers.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 158 (Book Page): The most important regulator of apoptosis is the TP53 tumour suppressor gene, often described as the ‘guardian of the genome’ as it is able to induce apoptosis in response to sufficient levels of genomic damage.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: Contrast the specific cancers caused by Hepatitis B/C versus Helicobacter pylori.
back: Hepatitis B/C: Hepatocellular carcinoma. H. pylori: Gastric MALT lymphomas and gastric cancer.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Viral infection... Hepatitis B and C viruses... Hepatocellular carcinoma. Bacterial infection... Helicobacter pylori... Gastric MALT lymphomas, gastric cancer.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: A woman from the Far East migrates to the West; why does her breast cancer risk increase?
back: Shift to Western lifestyle: high-fat/dairy diet, later first pregnancy, and obesity override her original low-risk genetic profile.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): risk of breast cancer in women of Far Eastern origin... rises in subsequent generations... factors that cause this change... may include diet... reproductive patterns... and lifestyle.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: Which specific dietary toxin is a major environmental determinant for hepatocellular carcinoma?
back: Aflatoxin (produced by Aspergillus flavus contamination of food supplies).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): association between aflatoxin production within contaminated food supplies and hepatocellular carcinomas.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: What is the estimated prevalence of inherited cancer syndromes among all cancer cases?
back: Inherited mutations in driver genes account for approximately 5%–10% of all cancers.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): A number of inherited cancer syndromes are recognised and account for 5%–10% of all cancers.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: Which Human Papillomavirus (HPV) subtypes are established as the primary environmental causes of cervical carcinoma?
back: HPV subtypes 16 and 18.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): most carcinomas of the cervix are related to infection with human papillomavirus (HPV subtypes 16 and 18).

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: Differentiate the primary driver gene mutations in Li–Fraumeni versus Cowden syndrome.
back: Li–Fraumeni: TP53. Cowden: PTEN.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 163 (Book Page): Li–Fraumeni syndrome... TP53. Cowden syndrome... PTEN.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: Explain the hormonal loop through which obesity increases risk for breast and endometrial cancers.
back: Obesity leads to increased endogenous oestrogen levels and elevated insulin production.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Obesity... increased insulin. Increased oestrogen... Breast and endometrial cancer.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: List three skin malignancies associated with the environmental factor of UV radiation.
back: Basal cell carcinoma, Melanoma, and Non-melanocytic skin cancer.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Radiation UV exposure... Basal cell carcinoma, Melanoma, Non-melanocytic skin cancer.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: What is the general etiology of most cancers regarding environmental and genetic interaction?
back: Result of a complex interaction between genetic factors and exposure to environmental carcinogens.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): The majority of cancers do not have a single cause but rather are the result of a complex interaction between genetic factors and exposure to environmental carcinogens.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: How do dietary factors and alcohol contribute to the global burden of cancer?
back:
- Account for 30% of global cancers
- Linked to stomach, colon, oesophagus, breast, and liver sites.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 158 (Book Page): Diet and alcohol contribute to a further 30% of cancers, including those of the stomach, colon, oesophagus, breast and liver.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Contrast the incidence and penetrance of inherited cancer syndromes vs. sporadic cases.
back:
- Incidence: 5%–10% of all cancers
- Penetrance: Greatly elevated risk but rarely 100% due to modulating factors.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): inherited cancer syndromes ... account for 5%–10% of all cancers ... none has 100% penetrance and additional modulating factors, both genetic and environmental, are likely to be operative.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: A woman from a low-risk country migrates to a high-risk Western country. How does her breast cancer risk change?
back: Risk rises in subsequent generations to approach the host population due to changes in diet and lifestyle.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): risk of breast cancer in women of Far Eastern origin ... rises in subsequent generations to approach that of the resident population of the host country.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Which specific occupational carcinogens are linked to Liver Angiosarcoma and Mesothelioma?
back:
- Liver Angiosarcoma: Vinyl chloride
- Mesothelioma: Asbestos
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Asbestos ... Lung cancer and mesothelioma; Vinyl chloride ... Liver angiosarcoma

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: List the three primary viral infections predisposing to Hepatocellular Carcinoma (HCC).
back:
1. Hepatitis B virus (HBV)
2. Hepatitis C virus (HCV)
3. Aflatoxin (Aspergillus contamination)
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Viral infection: Hepatitis B and C viruses ... Hepatocellular carcinoma; Dietary factors: Aflatoxin from contamination of Aspergillus flavus ... Hepatocellular cancer

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: What is the molecular basis of the 'driver mutations' seen in inherited syndromes?
back: Inherited mutations in genes regulating cell growth, cell death, and apoptosis.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): in general they result from inherited mutations in driver genes that regulate cell growth, cell death and apoptosis.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: A patient is identified as a BRCA1 carrier. What are the two primary clinical benefits of this genetic discovery?
back:
- Informs anti-cancer therapy decisions
- Enables preventative treatments (e.g., prophylactic mastectomy)
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): It may inform anti-cancer therapy decisions ... preventative treatments such as prophylactic mastectomy in women who carry a BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Which metabolic mechanism explains how obesity acts as an environmental risk for colon and breast cancer?
back: Increased insulin levels and increased oestrogen production.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Obesity: Reduced physical activity, increased insulin; Increased oestrogen ... Colon cancer; Breast and endometrial cancer

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Identify the primary environmental infection and subtype linked to Cervical Cancer.
back: Human Papillomavirus (HPV), specifically subtypes 16 and 18.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): most carcinomas of the cervix are related to infection with human papillomavirus (HPV subtypes 16 and 18).

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
coreConcept: Impact of Smoking on Cancer Mortality
front: Q: What percentage of global cancer deaths are attributed to cigarette smoking and its impact on lung cancer?
back:
• Accounts for >20% of all global cancer deaths.
• Responsible for 80% of lung cancers in men.
• Responsible for 50% of lung cancers in women.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 158 (Book Page): Cigarette smoking accounts for more than 20% of all global cancer deaths, 80% of lung cancer cases in men and 50% of lung cancer cases in women worldwide.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: Which infectious agents are major environmental determinants for 15% of cancers worldwide?
back:
• HPV: Cervical/Anal cancer.
• HBV and HCV: Hepatocellular carcinoma.
• Helicobacter pylori: Gastric cancer/MALT lymphoma.
• EBV: Burkitt lymphoma/Nasopharyngeal cancer.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 158 (Book Page): Infections account for a further 15% of cancers... including those of the cervix, stomach, liver, nasopharynx, anus and bladder.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: What are the primary dietary and lifestyle modifications suggested to reduce the 30% cancer risk they contribute?
back:
• Avoidance: Animal fat, red meat, alcohol, and obesity.
• Increase: Fiber, fresh fruit, vegetable intake, and physical activity.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 158 (Book Page): Diet and alcohol contribute to a further 30% of cancers... Lifestyle modification could reduce these if steps were taken to avoid animal fat and red meat, reduce alcohol, increase fibre, fresh fruit and vegetable intake, avoid obesity and increase physical activity.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: A 40-year-old worker with chronic benzene exposure is at high risk for which specific malignancy?
back:
• Acute myeloid leukaemia (AML).
• Mechanism: Occupational chemical exposure to petroleum industry derivatives.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Petroleum industry (benzene) [leads to] Acute leukaemia.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: What is the molecular basis and overall prevalence of inherited cancer syndromes?
back:
• Prevalence: 5%–10% of all cancers.
• Basis: Inherited mutations in driver genes regulating cell growth, cell death, and apoptosis.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): A number of inherited cancer syndromes are recognised and account for 5%–10% of all cancers... in general they result from inherited mutations in driver genes that regulate cell growth, cell death and apoptosis.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: List the hallmark cancers associated with Li–Fraumeni syndrome and the involved gene.
back:
• Gene: TP53.
• Malignancies: Sarcoma, breast cancer, osteosarcoma, leukaemia, and glioma.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 163 (Book Page): Li–Fraumeni syndrome [Malignancies]: Sarcoma, breast, osteosarcoma, leukaemia, glioma, adrenocortical. [Gene]: TP53.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: How does migration from the Far East to Western countries alter the genetic risk for breast cancer?
back:
• Initial risk: Remains low (matches country of origin).
• Later risk: Rises in subsequent generations to match host country.
• Causes: Changes in diet, reproductive patterns, and lifestyle.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): The risk of breast cancer in women of Far Eastern origin remains relatively low when they first migrate... but rises in subsequent generations to approach that of the resident population of the host country.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: Differentiate the malignancies associated with BRCA1/2 versus HNPCC (Lynch Syndrome).
back:
• BRCA1/2: Breast, ovarian, prostatic, and pancreatic cancers.
• HNPCC: Colonic, endometrial, ovarian, and gastric cancers.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 163 (Book Page): [Syndrome] Breast/ovarian [Gene] BRCA1, BRCA2; [Syndrome] Hereditary non-polyposis colon cancer (HNPCC) [Gene] MSH2, MLH1, MSH6, PMS1, PMS2.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: How does obesity contribute to colon, breast, and endometrial cancer development?
back:
• Mechanism 1: Increased insulin levels.
• Mechanism 2: Increased oestrogen production.
• Result: Promotion of cellular proliferation in hormonal and metabolic-sensitive tissues.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Obesity [Process]: Reduced physical activity, increased insulin, increased oestrogen. [Diseases]: Colon cancer, breast and endometrial cancer.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: What environmental factor specifically causes hepatocellular carcinoma via contaminated food supplies?
back:
• Aflatoxin.
• Source: Contamination by Aspergillus flavus in food storage.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Aflatoxin from contamination of Aspergillus flavus [leads to] Hepatocellular cancer.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: What percentage of global cancer deaths is attributed to cigarette smoking?
back: More than 20% of all global cancer deaths (including 80% of lung cancer cases in men).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 158 (Book Page): Cigarette smoking accounts for more than 20% of all global cancer deaths, 80% of lung cancer cases in men and 50% of lung cancer cases in women worldwide.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: How do dietary factors and alcohol consumption contribute to global cancer incidence?
back: They contribute to approximately 30% of cancers, specifically affecting the stomach, colon, liver, and breast.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 158 (Book Page): Diet and alcohol contribute to a further 30% of cancers, including those of the stomach, colon, oesophagus, breast and liver.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: What is the biological role of the TP53 gene in preventing genetic instability?
back: Known as the 'guardian of the genome', it induces apoptosis in response to DNA damage (cytotoxics, UV, or oxidative stress).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 160 (Book Page): The most important regulator of apoptosis is the TP53 tumour suppressor gene, often described as the ‘guardian of the genome’ as it is able to induce apoptosis in response to sufficient levels of genomic damage.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Contrast the cancer risk of Far Eastern migrants vs. subsequent generations regarding breast cancer.
back: Initial risk is low, but rises in later generations to match the host country due to Western lifestyle factors (diet, reproductive patterns).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): The risk of breast cancer in women of Far Eastern origin remains relatively low when they first migrate to a country with a Western lifestyle, but rises in subsequent generations to approach that of the resident population.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Which specific environmental carcinogen and infection are the primary triggers for hepatocellular carcinoma?
back:
1. Aflatoxin (contaminated food).
2. Hepatitis B and C viruses.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): association between aflatoxin production within contaminated food supplies and hepatocellular carcinomas... Page 162 (Book Page): Viral infection: Hepatitis B and C viruses; Disease: Hepatocellular carcinoma.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: What percentage of all cancers are estimated to arise from inherited cancer syndromes?
back: 5%–10% of all cancers.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): A number of inherited cancer syndromes are recognised and account for 5%–10% of all cancers.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Name the gene and inheritance pattern associated with Li–Fraumeni syndrome.
back:
Gene: TP53.
Pattern: Autosomal Dominant (AD).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 163 (Book Page): Table 7.2: Li–Fraumeni syndrome; Malignancies: Sarcoma, breast... Inheritance: AD; Gene: TP53.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: A patient with multiple colonic polyps and a family history of colon cancer likely has which gene mutation?
back: APC or MUTYH (Familial Adenomatous Polyposis).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 163 (Book Page): Familial adenomatous polyposis; Malignancies: Colonic, upper gastrointestinal tract; Inheritance: AD; Gene: APC, MUTYH.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: What two biological mechanisms link obesity specifically to breast and endometrial cancer risk?
back:
1. Increased oestrogen levels.
2. Reduced physical activity and increased insulin.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Box 7.1: Obesity; Processes: Reduced physical activity, increased insulin; Increased oestrogen; Diseases: Colon cancer; Breast and endometrial cancer.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: How do HPV subtypes 16 and 18 contribute to cervical cancer development?
back: They act as principal environmental infectious triggers for the majority of cervical carcinomas.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): Most carcinomas of the cervix are related to infection with human papillomavirus (HPV subtypes 16 and 18).

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Which environmental factor causes 80% of lung cancer in men and 20% of global cancer deaths?
back: Cigarette smoking. It is the primary preventable cause of global cancer mortality through carcinogen exposure.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 158 (Book Page): Cigarette smoking accounts for more than 20% of all global cancer deaths, 80% of lung cancer cases in men and 50% of lung cancer cases in women worldwide.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Explain the role of the TP53 gene as the 'guardian of the genome.'
back: It is a tumour suppressor that induces apoptosis in response to DNA damage, oxidative injury, or UV radiation.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 158 (Book Page): The most important regulator of apoptosis is the TP53 tumour suppressor gene, often described as the ‘guardian of the genome’ as it is able to induce apoptosis in response to sufficient levels of genomic damage.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Contrast the genetic origin of sporadic versus inherited cancer syndromes.
back: ● Sporadic: Acquired random somatic mutations/driver aberrations (90-95%). ● Inherited: Germline mutations in driver genes regulating growth/apoptosis (5-10%).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 158 (Book Page)/161: Multistep carcinogenesis results from successive clonal expansions... each expansion being triggered by acquisition of a random driver aberration... inherited cancer syndromes... account for 5%–10% of all cancers.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Identify the genetic mutation and associated cancers in Lynch Syndrome (HNPCC).
back: ● Mutation: DNA mismatch repair genes (MSH2, MLH1, MSH6, PMS1/2). ● Cancers: Colonic, endometrial, ovarian, and gastric.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 163 (Book Page): Hereditary non-polyposis colon cancer (HNPCC): Colonic, endometrial, ovarian, pancreatic, gastric; AD; MSH2, MLH1, MSH6, PMS1, PMS2.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: What are two management options for women carrying BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutations?
back: ● High-frequency screening for early detection. ● Prophylactic treatments like bilateral mastectomy or salpingo-oophorectomy.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): Patients... may also benefit from screening investigations to detect cancer early, or preventative treatments such as prophylactic mastectomy in women who carry a BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutation.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: List the associated cancers for HPV 16/18 and Helicobacter pylori infection.
back: ● HPV 16/18: Cervical, anal, and oropharyngeal carcinomas. ● H. pylori: Gastric adenocarcinoma and gastric MALT lymphomas.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Human papillomavirus: Cervical cancer, anal cancer, oropharyngeal cancer. Helicobacter pylori: Gastric MALT lymphomas, gastric cancer.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: By what mechanism does obesity increase the risk of breast and endometrial cancer?
back: Through elevated levels of circulating oestrogen (peripheral conversion) and increased insulin production.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Obesity: Reduced physical activity, increased insulin; Increased oestrogen; Colon cancer; Breast and endometrial cancer.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Differentiate between the occupational cancers caused by asbestos and vinyl chloride.
back: ● Asbestos: Lung cancer and Mesothelioma. ● Vinyl Chloride (PVC): Liver angiosarcoma.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Asbestos mining... (asbestos): Lung cancer and mesothelioma. Vinyl chloride (PVC) manufacturing: Liver angiosarcoma.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Define the 'Angiogenic Switch' in tumor development.
back: The persistent activation of pro-angiogenic factors (VEGF/PDGF) over inhibitors, allowing tumors to grow beyond 1mm³.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 160 (Book Page): Tumours... are unable to grow beyond 1 mm 3 without stimulating the development of a vascular supply... an angiogenic switch is activated and remains on.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Which dietary changes reduce the risk of colorectal and stomach cancers?
back: ● Reduce red meat and animal fat intake. ● Increase fiber, fresh fruit, and vegetable consumption.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 158 (Book Page): Lifestyle modification could reduce these if steps were taken to avoid animal fat and red meat, reduce alcohol, increase fibre, fresh fruit and vegetable intake.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: What percentage of global cancer deaths is attributed to cigarette smoking?
back:
- More than 20% of all global cancer deaths.
- Accounts for 80% of lung cancer in men and 50% in women.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 158 (Book Page): Cigarette smoking accounts for more than 20% of all global cancer deaths, 80% of lung cancer cases in men and 50% of lung cancer cases in women worldwide.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: Why is the TP53 gene described as the 'guardian of the genome'?
back:
- Induces apoptosis in response to DNA damage.
- Mutations are found in over half of all human cancers.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 158 (Book Page): TP53 tumour suppressor gene, often described as the 'guardian of the genome' as it is able to induce apoptosis in response to sufficient levels of genomic damage... Mutations in the TP53 gene are found in over half of cancers.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: Contrast the occupational triggers for Bladder cancer versus Liver Angiosarcoma.
back:
- Bladder Cancer: Dye and rubber manufacturing (aromatic amines).
- Liver Angiosarcoma: Vinyl chloride (PVC) manufacturing.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Dye and rubber manufacturing (aromatic amines) Bladder cancer... Vinyl chloride (PVC) manufacturing Liver angiosarcoma.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: A woman with BRCA1 mutation seeks advice. Which cancers is she at highest risk for?
back:
- Breast cancer.
- Ovarian cancer.
- Colonic, prostatic, and pancreatic cancers (elevated risk).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 163 (Book Page): Breast/ovarian Breast, ovarian, colonic, prostatic, pancreatic AD BRCA1, BRCA2.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: What is the primary role of Telomerase in enabling replicative immortality?
back:
- Adds nucleotides to telomeres.
- Prevents telomere shortening and premature arrest of cell division (senescence).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 159 (Book Page): Telomerase, a specialised polymerase enzyme, adds nucleotides to telomeres, allowing continued cell division and thus preventing premature arrest of cellular replication.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: List the specific infections associated with Burkitt lymphoma and Gastric MALT lymphoma.
back:
- Burkitt Lymphoma: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV).
- Gastric MALT Lymphoma: Helicobacter pylori (bacterial infection).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Epstein–Barr virus Burkitt lymphoma... Helicobacter pylori Gastric MALT lymphomas, gastric cancer.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: Explain the 'Aerobic Glycolysis' (Warburg Effect) paradox in cancer cells.
back:
- Cells use glycolysis even in the presence of oxygen.
- Though less ATP efficient, it provides intermediates for biosynthetic pathways (nucleosides/amino acids).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): Cancer cells can reprogram their glucose metabolism to limit energy production to glycolysis, even in the presence of oxygen. This has been termed ‘aerobic glycolysis’.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: Distinguish Li-Fraumeni syndrome from Lynch syndrome (HNPCC) based on genetic mutation.
back:
- Li-Fraumeni: Inherited mutation in TP53.
- Lynch Syndrome: Mutations in mismatch repair genes (MSH2, MLH1, MSH6, PMS1/2).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 163 (Book Page): Li–Fraumeni syndrome... AD TP53... Hereditary non-polyposis colon cancer (HNPCC)... AD MSH2, MLH1, MSH6, PMS1, PMS2.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: How does chronic inflammation contribute to the Hallmarks of Cancer?
back:
- Immune cells release Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) which are mutagenic.
- Release of cytokines and growth factors promotes angiogenesis and invasion.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): In particular, the release of reactive oxygen species, which are actively mutagenic, will accelerate the genetic evolution of surrounding cancer cells, enhancing growth and contributing to cancer progression.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Q: Which specific dietary contaminant is linked to Hepatocellular Carcinoma in developing nations?
back:
- Aflatoxin.
- Produced by Aspergillus flavus contaminating food supplies.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): The association between aflatoxin production within contaminated food supplies and hepatocellular carcinomas.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: What does the T, N, and M represent in the UICC standard staging classification?
back:
- T: Size or depth of the primary tumour.
- N: Involvement of regional lymph nodes.
- M: Presence or absence of distant metastases.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 163 (Book Page): [The outcome is recorded using a standard staging classification... One of the most commonly used systems is the T (tumour), N (regional lymph nodes), M (metastatic sites) approach]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Which imaging modality is the preferred technique for staging malignancies of the brain, bone, and pelvis?
back:
- Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).
- It is chosen for its high resolution in these specific anatomical sites.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): [Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has a high resolution and is the preferred technique for brain, bone and pelvic imaging.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: How is a 'Partial Response' (PR) defined according to the RECIST criteria?
back:
- At least a 30% decrease in the sum of the longest diameter (LD) of target lesions.
- Baseline sum LD is used as the reference.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 176 (Book Page): [Partial response (PR): At least a 30% decrease in the sum of the longest diameter (LD) of target lesions, taking as reference the baseline sum LD]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: What is the clinical significance of molecular testing for RAS mutations in colorectal cancer?
back:
- RAS mutations predict resistance to EGFR inhibitor targeted therapy (e.g., cetuximab).
- It guides the selection of appropriate systemic therapy.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): [RAS mutations – predict resistance to EGFR inhibitor targeted therapy in colon cancer]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Identify two microscopic findings on light microscopy that suggest a gastric primary or melanoma respectively.
back:
- Gastric primary: Presence of signet-ring cells.
- Melanoma: Presence of melanin.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 164 (Book Page): [Signet-ring cells favour a gastric primary. Presence of melanin favours melanoma.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: List three non-malignant clinical conditions that can cause an elevation in serum CA-125 levels.
back:
- Ascites (any cause).
- Pleural effusion.
- Heart failure or inflammatory conditions.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 164 (Book Page): [Raised in any cause of ascites, pleural effusion or heart failure. Can be raised in inflammatory conditions]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Explain the role of Immunohistochemistry (IHC) for ER, PR, and HER2 in breast cancer management.
back:
- ER/PR positivity: Predicts sensitivity to hormonal manipulation.
- HER2 positivity: Indicates suitability for HER2 inhibitor targeted therapy (e.g., trastuzumab).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): [Oestrogen (ER) and progesterone (PR) receptor positivity indicate that the cancer may be sensitive to hormonal manipulation... HER2 receptor positivity... indicate that the tumour may respond to HER2 inhibitor targeted therapy.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
coreConcept: Investigation of Midline Germ Cell Tumours
front: A young man presents with a midline metastatic tumour of unknown primary; which investigations are critical to exclude treatable disease?
back:
- Testicular ultrasound.
- Serum Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP).
- Serum Human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 167 (Book Page): [Tumour markers... α-fetoprotein (AFP) and human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG) in midline disease in young men... Testicular ultrasound (if midline disease in young man...)]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: What is a major physiological limitation of PET-CT in the assessment of lymph node involvement?
back:
- Limited sensitivity for small malignant nodes.
- Metabolic activity in very small clusters of cancer cells may not be detectable.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): [The metabolic activity of small but malignant lymph nodes may not be detected, limiting the sensitivity of PET-CT.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Briefly distinguish between the three methods of obtaining a tissue diagnosis: Cytology, FNA, and Core Biopsy.
back:
- Cytology: Examination of cells from fluids (e.g., pleural) or smears.
- FNA: Aspiration of cells from a palpable lump via negative pressure.
- Core Biopsy: Histological examination of a tissue segment for architecture.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 163 (Book Page): [diagnosis can be obtained by examination of cells (cytology) from fluid... or by doing fine needle aspiration... Core biopsy of the most accessible metastatic lesion is usually the quickest way of obtaining tissue for pathological evaluation]

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: What percentage of global cancer deaths is attributed to cigarette smoking?
back: Smoking accounts for over 20% of all global cancer deaths, including 80% of lung cancer cases in men and 50% in women.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 158 (Book Page): Cigarette smoking accounts for more than 20% of all global cancer deaths, 80% of lung cancer cases in men and 50% of lung cancer cases in women worldwide.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: How do environmental and genetic factors typically interact in the pathogenesis of cancer?
back: Most cancers result from a complex interaction between genetic predisposition and environmental carcinogens rather than a single isolated cause.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): The majority of cancers do not have a single cause but rather are the result of a complex interaction between genetic factors and exposure to environmental carcinogens.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Contrast the cancer associations of Human Papillomavirus (HPV) with Hepatitis B and C viruses.
back: HPV (subtypes 16/18): Cervical, anal, and oropharyngeal cancers. HBV/HCV: Hepatocellular carcinoma.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Human papillomavirus: Cervical cancer, anal cancer, oropharyngeal cancer. Hepatitis B and C viruses: Hepatocellular carcinoma.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Why do carriers of inherited driver gene mutations, like BRCA1, not always develop cancer?
back: These mutations have incomplete penetrance; additional genetic modulators and environmental factors are required to trigger malignancy.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): Although carriers of these gene mutations have a greatly elevated risk of cancer, none has 100% penetrance and additional modulating factors, both genetic and environmental, are likely to be operative.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: What role does vaccination play in preventing environmental-related cancers in developing countries?
back: Infections cause 25% of cancers in low-income countries. Vaccination against HPV and HBV can prevent significant portions of these cases.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 158 (Book Page): Infections account for a further 15% of cancers (25% of cancers in low- and middle-income countries)... some of these could be prevented by infection control and vaccination.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Match the following occupational exposures to their specific malignancies: Asbestos and Benzene.
back: Asbestos: Lung cancer and mesothelioma. Benzene: Acute leukaemia.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Asbestos mining, construction work, shipbuilding (asbestos): Lung cancer and mesothelioma. Petroleum industry (benzene): Acute leukaemia.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Apply the concept of epigenomic aberrations to cancer development beyond direct DNA sequence changes.
back: Epigenomic changes like DNA methylation and histone modification can confer survival advantages and drive clonal expansion in pre-malignant cells.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 158 (Book Page): Epigenomic aberrations, such as DNA methylation and histone modification, may also occur... conferring a selective survival advantage on single cells, 'driving' overgrowth.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Which specific inherited syndrome is caused by TP53 mutations and what is its inheritance pattern?
back: Li–Fraumeni syndrome. It is an Autosomal Dominant (AD) condition associated with sarcomas, breast cancer, and leukaemias.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 163 (Book Page): Li–Fraumeni syndrome: Sarcoma, breast, osteosarcoma, leukaemia, glioma, adrenocortical... AD... TP53.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Identify the metabolic triad through which obesity promotes the development of colon and breast cancers.
