back: 1. Reduced physical activity. 2. Increased insulin levels. 3. Increased oestrogen production.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Obesity: Reduced physical activity, increased insulin, Increased oestrogen. Diseases: Colon cancer, Breast and endometrial cancer.

category: Discuss the role of environmental and genetic factors in cancer development
front: Which dietary modifications are clinically recommended to reduce the risk of gastrointestinal and breast cancers?
back: Avoidance of animal fats/red meat, reducing alcohol, and increasing fiber, fresh fruit, and vegetable intake.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 158 (Book Page): Lifestyle modification could reduce these if steps were taken to avoid animal fat and red meat, reduce alcohol, increase fibre, fresh fruit and vegetable intake.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: What is the primary role of PET-CT in cancer staging and management?
back: Visualises metabolic activity of tumour cells. Essential for evaluating distant metastases when considering radical/curative treatment options.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): [Positron emission tomography (PET) visualises metabolic activity of tumour cells and is often used in combination with CT (PET–CT) to evaluate the extent of the disease, particularly in the assessment of potential distant metastases when a radical treatment approach is being considered.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: How do RAS mutations influence the management of metastatic colon cancer?
back: Predict resistance to EGFR inhibitor targeted therapies (e.g., cetuximab). Used as a molecular marker to exclude unsuitable patients from specific treatments.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): [RAS mutations – predict resistance to EGFR inhibitor targeted therapy in colon cancer]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Contrast the diagnostic utility of CT versus MRI in oncological imaging.
back: CT: Preferred for thorax and abdomen imaging. MRI: Higher resolution for brain, bone, and pelvic (rectal, cervical, prostate) staging.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): [Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has a high resolution and is the preferred technique for brain, bone and pelvic imaging. ... Computed tomography (CT) is a key investigation ... particularly useful in imaging the thorax and abdomen]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Which investigations are prioritized for a young male presenting with a suspicious midline mass?
back: Serum Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and hCG levels. Testicular ultrasound. Biopsy for histology.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 167 (Book Page): [hCG and AFP suggestive of a non-seminomatous testicular cancer ... Testicular ultrasound (if midline disease in young man or clinical features suggest germ cell tumour)]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Define the role of Immunohistochemistry (IHC) for HER2 in breast cancer management.
back: Determines over-expression of HER2 receptor. Identifies patients likely to respond to targeted therapies like Trastuzumab (Herceptin).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): [HER2 receptor positivity in breast or gastric cancers indicate that the tumour may respond to HER2 inhibitor targeted therapy.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: According to RECIST, what constitutes 'Progressive Disease' (PD) during treatment evaluation?
back: ≥20% increase in the sum of longest diameters (LD) of target lesions. Minimum 5mm absolute increase or appearance of new lesions.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 176 (Book Page): [At least a 20% increase in the sum of the LD of target lesions, taking as reference the smallest sum LD recorded since the treatment started and at least 5 mm increase or the appearance of one or more new lesions]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: How is Cytogenetic analysis (FISH) specifically applied in the diagnosis of Ewing's sarcoma?
back: Detects the specific chromosomal translocation t(11;22)(q24;q12). Differentiates it from other small round blue cell tumors.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): [utilisation of fluorescent in situ hybridisation (FISH) techniques can be useful in Ewing's sarcoma ... where there is a translocation between chromosome 11 and 22: t(11;22)(q24;q12).]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: What is the investigation of choice for managing suspected metastatic bone disease?
back: Isotope bone scan (high sensitivity). Plain X-ray or MRI for symptomatic/lytic areas (higher specificity than bone scan for myeloma).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 172 (Book Page): [The most sensitive way of detecting bone metastases is by isotope bone scan. ... Plain X-ray films or MRI scans are therefore preferred for any sites of bone pain, as lytic lesions may not be detected by a bone scan.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Contrast the management roles of CA-125 in diagnosis versus monitoring.
back: Diagnosis: Non-specific; raised in any cause of ascites or inflammation. Monitoring: Used to track treatment response and detect recurrence in epithelial ovarian cancer.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 164 (Book Page): [CA-125... Raised in any cause of ascites, pleural effusion or heart failure. ... Ovarian epithelial cancer (75%)]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Which tumor marker is essential for screening in Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia (MEN) 2?
back: Serum Calcitonin. Produced by C-cells of the thyroid and diagnostic for Medullary Cell Carcinoma.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 164 (Book Page): [Calcitonin ... 32-amino-acid peptide from C cells of thyroid. Used to screen for MEN 2]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: What is the primary role of Computed Tomography (CT) in initial cancer staging?
back:
• Preferred for imaging the thorax and abdomen
• Visualizes primary tumour and local/regional spread
• Used for CT colonography to detect lesions ≥10mm
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): [Computed tomography (CT) is a key investigation in cancer patients and is particularly useful in imaging the thorax and abdomen... visualize the large bowel... detection of colorectal cancers and adenomas ≥ 10 mm.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: How does Positron Emission Tomography (PET) differ from traditional imaging in cancer assessment?
back:
• Visualizes metabolic activity of cells rather than just anatomy
• Typically combined with CT (PET-CT)
• Evaluates distant metastases before radical treatment decisions
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): [Positron emission tomography (PET) visualises metabolic activity of tumour cells and is often used in combination with CT (PET–CT) to evaluate the extent of the disease, particularly in the assessment of potential distant metastases when a radical treatment approach is being considered.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Which three anatomical sites are best imaged using Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) resolution?
back:
• Brain
• Bone
• Pelvis (specifically rectal, cervical, and prostate cancers)
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): [Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has a high resolution and is the preferred technique for brain, bone and pelvic imaging. It is widely employed for the staging of rectal, cervical and prostate cancers.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: A patient presents with ascites. Why should CA-125 levels be interpreted with caution?
back:
• CA-125 is non-specific to ovarian cancer
• Raised in any cause of ascites, pleural effusion, or heart failure
• Elevated in common inflammatory conditions
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 166 (Book Page): [Cancer antigen 125 (CA-125)... Raised in any cause of ascites, pleural effusion or heart failure. Can be raised in inflammatory conditions]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: What is the clinical significance of determining HER2 receptor status via immunohistochemistry?
back:
• Predicts response to HER2 inhibitor targeted therapy (e.g., trastuzumab)
• Essential for management planning in breast and gastric cancers
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): [HER2 receptor positivity in breast or gastric cancers indicate that the tumour may respond to HER2 inhibitor targeted therapy.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Which specific histological finding on light microscopy strongly suggests a gastric primary cancer?
back:
• Presence of Signet-ring cells
• Observed during histopathological analysis of tumour samples
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 164 (Book Page): [Signet-ring cells favour a gastric primary.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: How does molecular profiling for RAS mutations influence the management of colon cancer?
back:
• RAS mutations predict resistance to EGFR inhibitor targeted therapy
• Guides clinicians to avoid ineffective treatments in mutated cases
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): [RAS mutations – predict resistance to EGFR inhibitor targeted therapy in colon cancer]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: A young man presents with a bulky midline mass. Which two tumor markers are diagnostic priorities?
back:
• Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP)
• Human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG)
• Elevated levels suggest non-seminomatous germ cell tumours
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 167 (Book Page): [Tumour markers: ... α-fetoprotein (AFP) and human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG) in midline disease in young men]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Why must serum calcium be adjusted for albumin when investigating malignancy-associated hypercalcaemia?
back:
• Hypoalbuminaemia is common in cancer patients
• Total calcium values underestimate the level of active (ionised) calcium
• Essential for accurate metabolic assessment
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 170 (Book Page): [It is especially important to correct for albumin in cancer because hypoalbuminaemia is common and total calcium values under-estimate the level of ionised calcium.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Which cytogenetic technique and specific translocation identify Ewing's sarcoma?
back:
• Fluorescent in situ hybridisation (FISH)
• Translocation t(11;22)(q24;q12)
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): [FISH techniques can be useful in Ewing's sarcoma... where there is a translocation between chromosome 11 and 22: t(11;22)(q24;q12).]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: List the three primary clinical requirements to be established by investigations during cancer management planning.
back:
1. Extent of disease (staging).
2. Type of cancer (histology/cytology).
3. Patient’s fitness (performance status/comorbidities).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): [In order to plan the most appropriate investigations and management, information is needed on: the extent of disease, the type of cancer, the patient’s fitness.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Describe the diagnostic utility of Positron Emission Tomography (PET) in oncological staging.
back:
1. Visualises metabolic activity of tumour cells (often PET-CT).
2. Evaluates distant metastases before radical treatment.
3. Limitation: Not all tumour types are 'PET-avid'.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): [Positron emission tomography (PET) visualises metabolic activity of tumour cells and is often used in combination with CT (PET–CT) to evaluate the extent of the disease... Not all tumour types are ‘PET-avid’]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Differentiate the diagnostic significance of Psammoma bodies on light microscopy based on mucin status.
back:
1. Ovarian Cancer: Psammoma bodies present and Mucin positive (+).
2. Thyroid Cancer: Psammoma bodies present and Mucin negative (-).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): [Psammoma bodies are a feature of ovarian cancer (mucin +) and thyroid cancer (mucin -).]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: A lung adenocarcinoma patient tests positive for an ALK fusion oncogene. How does this influence management?
back:
1. Predicts response to ALK inhibitor targeted therapy.
2. Demonstrates the role of molecular profiling in tailoring 'druggable' pathway treatments.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): [ALK fusion oncogene rearrangement – predict response to ALK inhibitor targeted therapy in lung cancer... Treatment selection is increasingly tailored to specific ‘druggable’ molecular pathways]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Explain the clinical utility and common tumor associations for serum Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) markers.
back:
1. Ovarian non-seminomatous germ cell tumours (80%).
2. Testicular teratoma (80%).
3. Hepatocellular cancer (50%).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 164 (Book Page): [Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP)... Ovarian non-seminomatous germ cell tumours (80%), testicular teratoma (80%), hepatocellular cancer (50%)]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Define the RECIST criteria for 'Complete Response' and 'Partial Response' in treatment evaluation.
back:
1. Complete Response (CR): Disappearance of all target lesions.
2. Partial Response (PR): Minimum 30% decrease in the sum of longest diameters (LD) of target lesions.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 176 (Book Page): [Complete response (CR): Disappearance of all target lesions. Partial response (PR): At least a 30% decrease in the sum of the longest diameter (LD) of target lesions]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Contrast the sensitivity of isotope bone scans versus plain X-rays for Multiple Myeloma bone lesions.
back:
1. Isotope bone scan: Frequent false-negatives due to suppressed osteoblast activity.
2. Plain X-ray/MRI: Preferred for detecting lytic lesions in Myeloma.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 172 (Book Page): [Isotope bone scan... can have... false-negative results occur in multiple myeloma due to suppression of osteoblast activity. Plain X-ray films or MRI scans are therefore preferred for any sites of bone pain]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: A colon cancer patient shows a RAS mutation. How does this investigation impact the choice of EGFR-targeted therapy?
back:
1. Predicts resistance to EGFR inhibitor therapy (e.g., Cetuximab).
2. Mandates alternative treatment as the mutation bypasses EGFR blockade.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): [RAS mutations – predict resistance to EGFR inhibitor targeted therapy in colon cancer]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Explain the biochemical role and diagnostic associations of the CA-125 tumor marker.
back:
1. Differentiation antigen of coelomic epithelium.
2. Raised in 75% of ovarian epithelial cancers.
3. Also elevated in any cause of ascites, pleural effusion, or heart failure.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 164 (Book Page): [Cancer antigen 125 (CA-125)... Ovarian epithelial cancer (75%)... Raised in any cause of ascites, pleural effusion or heart failure.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Identify the likely primary tumors suggested by 'Signet-ring cells' and 'Melanin' on light microscopy.
back:
1. Signet-ring cells: Suggests a Gastric primary.
2. Melanin: Suggests Melanoma.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 164 (Book Page): [Signet-ring cells favour a gastric primary. Presence of melanin favours melanoma.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: What does the 'T', 'N', and 'M' represent in the UICC staging classification?
back:
- T: Extent of primary tumour size/depth.
- N: Regional lymph node involvement.
- M: Presence of distant metastases.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): One of the most commonly used systems is the T (tumour), N (regional lymph nodes), M (metastatic sites) approach of the International Union against Cancer (UICC, see Box 7.3).

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Which imaging modality is preferred for staging brain, bone, and pelvic malignancies?
back: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI). It offers the high resolution required for these specific anatomical sites.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has a high resolution and is the preferred technique for brain, bone and pelvic imaging.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: What is the primary clinical role of PET-CT in oncology staging?
back: Visualises metabolic activity to assess disease extent and distant metastases, especially before radical treatment.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Positron emission tomography (PET) visualises metabolic activity of tumour cells and is often used in combination with CT (PET–CT) to evaluate the extent of the disease, particularly in the assessment of potential distant metastases when a radical treatment approach is being considered.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
coreConcept: Biochemical Markers for Germ Cell Tumors
front: Q: Which serum tumor markers are essential for investigating suspected germ cell tumors in young men?
back:
- Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP)
- Human Chorionic Gonadotrophin (hCG)
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 167 (Book Page): Tumour markers: ... α-fetoprotein (AFP) and human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG) in midline disease in young men.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Define Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status Grade 4.
back: Completely disabled; unable to perform any self-care; totally confined to a bed or chair.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): 4 Completely disabled, unable to carry out any self-care and confined totally to bed or chair.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: On light microscopy, which findings favor a diagnosis of gastric cancer vs. melanoma?
back:
- Gastric: Signet-ring cells.
- Melanoma: Presence of melanin.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 164 (Book Page): Signet-ring cells favour a gastric primary. Presence of melanin favours melanoma.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Contrast the role of molecular mutations in lung vs. colon cancer regarding EGFR inhibitors.
back:
- Lung: EGFR mutations predict treatment response.
- Colon: RAS mutations predict treatment resistance.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): EGFR mutations – predict response to EGFR inhibitor targeted therapy in lung cancer; RAS mutations – predict resistance to EGFR inhibitor targeted therapy in colon cancer.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: What are the gold-standard investigations for SVCO and Malignant Spinal Cord Compression?
back:
- SVCO: CT scan of the thorax.
- Cord Compression: Urgent MRI of the whole spine.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 168 (Book Page): [Cord Compression] Confirm diagnosis with urgent MRI scan of whole spine. Page 169 (Book Page): [SVCO] The investigation of choice is a CT scan of the thorax to confirm the diagnosis.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Mention three IHC markers used to stratify breast cancer treatment.
back:
1. Oestrogen Receptor (ER)
2. Progesterone Receptor (PR)
3. HER2 Receptor
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): Oestrogen (ER) and progesterone (PR) receptor positivity indicate that the cancer may be sensitive to hormonal manipulation... HER2 receptor positivity in breast or gastric cancers indicate that the tumour may respond to HER2 inhibitor targeted therapy.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Which biochemical criteria confirm a pleural effusion is malignant/exudative?
back:
- Fluid-to-serum LDH ratio > 0.6
- Fluid-to-serum protein ratio > 0.5
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 172 (Book Page): Malignant effusions are commonly blood-stained and are exudates with a raised fluid to serum LDH ratio (> 0.6) and a raised fluid to serum protein ratio (>0.5).

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: In the TNM classification system, what specific parameters do 'T', 'N', and 'M' represent?
back:
• T: Extent/size of the primary tumour.
• N: Involvement of regional lymph nodes.
• M: Presence of distant metastases.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 163 (Book Page): [The outcome is recorded using a standard staging classification... One of the most commonly used systems is the T (tumour), N (regional lymph nodes), M (metastatic sites) approach].

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Why is MRI generally preferred over CT for staging cancers of the brain, bone, and pelvis?
back:
• High resolution for soft tissues.
• Preferred for staging rectal, cervical, and prostate cancers.
• Superior for identifying bone marrow involvement.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): [Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has a high resolution and is the preferred technique for brain, bone and pelvic imaging. It is widely employed for the staging of rectal, cervical and prostate cancers].

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: What is the primary role of Positron Emission Tomography (PET) in cancer management?
back:
• Visualizes the metabolic activity of tumour cells.
• Combined with CT (PET-CT) to evaluate the extent of disease/distant metastases.
• Used when radical treatment is being considered.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): [Positron emission tomography (PET) visualises metabolic activity of tumour cells and is often used in combination with CT (PET–CT) to evaluate the extent of the disease, particularly in the assessment of potential distant metastases].

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: A patient with colorectal cancer undergoes molecular profiling. What is the clinical significance of detecting a RAS mutation?
back:
• Predicts resistance to EGFR inhibitor targeted therapy (e.g., cetuximab).
• Prevents unnecessary use of ineffective treatment in patients with these mutations.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): [RAS mutations – predict resistance to EGFR inhibitor targeted therapy in colon cancer].

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Which serum tumour marker is specifically used for the screening and diagnosis of Medullary Cell Carcinoma of the thyroid?
back:
• Calcitonin (a 32-amino-acid peptide).
• Also used to screen for Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia (MEN) 2 syndrome.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 163 (Book Page): [Calcitonin: 32-amino-acid peptide from C cells of thyroid. Used to screen for MEN 2... Medullary cell carcinoma of thyroid].

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Which investigation is most sensitive for detecting bone metastases, and what are its common causes for false-negatives?
back:
• Most sensitive: Isotope bone scan.
• False-negative cause: Multiple myeloma (due to suppression of osteoblast activity).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 172 (Book Page): [The most sensitive way of detecting bone metastases is by isotope bone scan... false-negative results occur in multiple myeloma due to suppression of osteoblast activity].

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: According to RECIST criteria, what defines a 'Partial Response' (PR) to cancer treatment?
back:
• At least a 30% decrease in the sum of the longest diameters of target lesions.
• Calculated relative to the baseline sum longest diameter.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 176 (Book Page): [Partial response (PR): At least a 30% decrease in the sum of the longest diameter (LD) of target lesions, taking as reference the baseline sum LD].

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: How do biochemical investigations of albumin and C-reactive protein (CRP) assist in assessing a cancer patient's fitness?
back:
• Outcomes are significantly worse for patients with low albumin or raised inflammatory markers (CRP).
• Independent of performance status, these predict poor treatment tolerance.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): [outcomes are typically worse for patients with a low albumin and raised inflammatory markers (i.e. white blood cell count, C-reactive protein)].

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Which diagnostic technique is specifically used to classify lymphomas via antigen expression?
back:
• Immunohistochemistry (IHC).
• Identifies T-cell receptors and Cluster Designation (CD) antigen expression.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): [T-cell receptor and cluster designation (CD) antigen expression aid in the diagnosis and classification of lymphomas].

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: What diagnostic investigation is used to detect gene amplification, such as HER2 in breast cancer, when immunohistochemistry is inconclusive?
back:
• Fluorescent in situ hybridisation (FISH).
• Uses cytogenetic analysis to visualize specific chromosomal translocations or amplifications.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): [The utilisation of fluorescent in situ hybridisation (FISH) techniques can be useful... In some cases, gene amplification can be detected via FISH (e.g. determining over-expression of HER2/neu)].

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: What do the components of the UICC staging system (TNM) specifically represent?
back:
- T: Size or depth of primary tumour
- N: Involvement of regional lymph nodes
- M: Presence of distant metastases
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 163 (Book Page): [One of the most commonly used systems is the T (tumour), N (regional lymph nodes), M (metastatic sites) approach of the International Union against Cancer (UICC, see Box 7.3 ).]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: What is the primary diagnostic advantage of Positron Emission Tomography (PET) in cancer management?
back:
- Visualises metabolic activity of tumour cells
- Evaluates extent of disease, particularly distant metastases, before radical treatment
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): [Positron emission tomography (PET) visualises metabolic activity of tumour cells and is often used in combination with CT (PET–CT) to evaluate the extent of the disease, particularly in the assessment of potential distant metastases when a radical treatment approach is being considered.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: For which three specific anatomical sites is MRI preferred over CT for cancer staging?
back:
- Brain
- Bone
- Pelvis (including rectal, cervical, and prostate cancers)
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): [Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has a high resolution and is the preferred technique for brain, bone and pelvic imaging. It is widely employed for the staging of rectal, cervical and prostate cancers.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: In Cancer of Unknown Primary (CUP), which investigation is the most efficient for establishing the tumour type?
back:
- Core biopsy of the most accessible metastatic lesion
- Enables histological, immunohistochemical, and molecular pathology evaluation
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 167 (Book Page): [If patients are fit to undergo investigations and fit enough to be considered for treatment then a core biopsy of the most accessible metastatic lesion is usually the quickest way of obtaining tissue for pathological evaluation of cancer type.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: What is the clinical role of molecular profiling for EGFR mutations in lung cancer?
back:
- Predicts response to EGFR inhibitor targeted therapy (e.g., gefitinib, erlotinib)
- Guides personalized treatment selection
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): [EGFR mutations – predict response to EGFR inhibitor targeted therapy in lung cancer]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: What is the specific utility of CT colonography in the investigation of colorectal cancer?
back:
- Accurate detection of colorectal cancers
- Identifies adenomas ≥ 10 mm in size in prepared bowels
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): [With modern scanners it is possible to visualise the large bowel if it is prepared (CT colonography), allowing accurate detection of colorectal cancers and adenomas ≥ 10 mm.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Why are serum tumour markers generally not used in isolation for primary cancer diagnosis?
back:
- Lacks sufficient sensitivity and specificity
- Must be interpreted alongside clinical features and imaging results
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 163 (Book Page): [Unfortunately, most tumour markers are neither sufficiently sensitive nor sufficiently specific to be used in isolation for diagnosis and need to be interpreted in the context of other clinical features.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Which investigation is mandatory for confirming a diagnosis of malignant spinal cord compression?
back:
- Urgent MRI scan of the whole spine
- Used to identify the level and degree of compression
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 168 (Book Page): [Confirm diagnosis with urgent MRI scan of whole spine]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Why must serum total calcium be adjusted for albumin when investigating hypercalcaemia of malignancy?
back:
- Hypoalbuminaemia is common in cancer patients
- Unadjusted total calcium values underestimate the level of active ionised calcium
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 170 (Book Page): [It is especially important to correct for albumin in cancer because hypoalbuminaemia is common and total calcium values under-estimate the level of ionised calcium.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: How does HER2 immunohistochemistry (IHC) influence the management of breast and gastric cancers?
back:
- Positive status indicates suitability for HER2 inhibitor targeted therapy (e.g., trastuzumab)
- Identifies aggressive biological subtypes for tailored treatment
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): [HER2 receptor positivity in breast or gastric cancers indicate that the tumour may respond to HER2 inhibitor targeted therapy.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Define the T, N, and M components of the standard International Union against Cancer (UICC) staging system.
back:
- T: Size or depth of invasion of the primary tumour.
- N: Extent of regional lymph node involvement.
- M: Presence or absence of distant metastases.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 163 (Book Page): [The outcome is recorded using a standard staging classification... One of the most commonly used systems is the T (tumour), N (regional lymph nodes), M (metastatic sites) approach of the International Union against Cancer (UICC)]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Why is PET-CT specifically utilized during the assessment for radical (curative) cancer treatment?
back:
- Evaluates the metabolic activity of tumour cells.
- High sensitivity for detecting distant metastases that may preclude radical surgery.
- Combines functional metabolic data with anatomical CT imaging.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 164 (Book Page): [PET–CT to evaluate the extent of the disease, particularly in the assessment of potential distant metastases when a radical treatment approach is being considered.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Contrast the primary anatomical staging indications for MRI versus CT imaging.
back:
- MRI: Preferred for high-resolution imaging of the brain, bone, and pelvic organs (rectum/prostate).
- CT: Key investigation for imaging the thorax and abdomen.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 164 (Book Page): [Computed tomography (CT) is... particularly useful in imaging the thorax and abdomen... Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has a high resolution and is the preferred technique for brain, bone and pelvic imaging.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: A young man presents with a midline mediastinal mass and unknown primary; which serum markers are diagnostic priorities?
back:
- Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP).
- Human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG).
- Essential to identify highly treatable germ cell tumours.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 167 (Book Page): [Testicular ultrasound (if midline disease in young man or clinical features suggest germ cell tumour)... α-fetoprotein (AFP) and human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG) in midline disease in young men]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: How does molecular testing for RAS mutations affect the management of colorectal cancer patients?
back:
- Predicts resistance to EGFR inhibitor targeted therapies (e.g., cetuximab/panitumumab).
- Ensures targeted therapy is only given to patients with RAS wild-type tumours.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): [RAS mutations – predict resistance to EGFR inhibitor targeted therapy in colon cancer]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: List the four standard categories used in RECIST to evaluate solid tumour response to systemic therapy.
back:
- Complete Response (CR): Disappearance of all lesions.
- Partial Response (PR): ≥30% decrease in sum of diameters.
- Stable Disease (SD): Insufficient shrinkage for PR or increase for PD.
- Progressive Disease (PD): ≥20% increase in sum of diameters.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 176 (Book Page): [Box 7.19 Response evaluation criteria in solid tumours (RECIST)]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Which specific microscopic histopathological features suggest a gastric vs. ovarian primary in metastatic adenocarcinoma?
back:
- Gastric: Signet-ring cells.
- Ovarian: Psammoma bodies (also found in thyroid cancer) and Mucin positivity.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 164 (Book Page): [Signet-ring cells favour a gastric primary... Psammoma bodies are a feature of ovarian cancer (mucin +) and thyroid cancer (mucin -).]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Why is a conventional isotope bone scan unreliable for assessing skeletal involvement in Multiple Myeloma?
back:
- Myeloma suppresses osteoblast activity.
- Isotope scans rely on osteoblastic 'flare' for detection.
- Results in false-negatives; MRI or plain X-rays (for lytic lesions) are preferred.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 172 (Book Page): [false-negative results occur in multiple myeloma due to suppression of osteoblast activity. Plain X-ray films or MRI scans are therefore preferred for any sites of bone pain, as lytic lesions may not be detected by a bone scan.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Why must serum total calcium be adjusted for albumin levels in cancer patients?
back:
- Hypoalbuminaemia is highly common in cancer.
- Total calcium measurements underestimate the physiologically active ionised calcium.
- Necessary to accurately diagnose Hypercalcaemia of Malignancy.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 170 (Book Page): [It is especially important to correct for albumin in cancer because hypoalbuminaemia is common and total calcium values under-estimate the level of ionised calcium.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: List three non-malignant clinical conditions that can cause a rise in the serum tumour marker CA-125.
back:
- Any cause of ascites (e.g., cirrhosis).
- Pleural effusion or heart failure.
- Pelvic inflammatory conditions.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 164 (Book Page): [Raised in any cause of ascites, pleural effusion or heart failure. Can be raised in inflammatory conditions]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: What is the primary role of PET-CT in the staging of cancer patients?
back: It visualises metabolic activity to evaluate disease extent, specifically for detecting distant metastases when radical treatment is considered.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 134 (Book Page): Positron emission tomography (PET) visualises metabolic activity of tumour cells and is often used in combination with CT (PET–CT) to evaluate the extent of the disease, particularly in the assessment of potential distant metastases when a radical treatment approach is being considered.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: How do Immunohistochemistry (IHC) markers for ER/PR and HER2 guide management in breast cancer?
back: 1. ER/PR positivity: Predicts sensitivity to hormonal manipulation. 2. HER2 positivity: Predicts response to targeted therapy (HER2 inhibitors).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 137 (Book Page): Oestrogen (ER) and progesterone (PR) receptor positivity indicate that the cancer may be sensitive to hormonal manipulation... HER2 receptor positivity in breast or gastric cancers indicate that the tumour may respond to HER2 inhibitor targeted therapy.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: For which specific anatomical regions is MRI preferred over CT for cancer staging?
back: MRI has high resolution and is the preferred technique for brain, bone, and pelvic (rectal, cervical, and prostate) imaging.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 134 (Book Page): Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has a high resolution and is the preferred technique for brain, bone and pelvic imaging. It is widely employed for the staging of rectal, cervical and prostate cancers.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: A patient has metastatic adenocarcinoma of unknown primary. List four essential initial biochemical investigations.
back: 1. Full blood count; 2. Liver and renal function tests; 3. Serum calcium; 4. Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) and C-reactive protein (CRP).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 139 (Book Page): Initial diagnostic tests in patients presenting with carcinoma of unknown primary... Full blood count, urea and electrolytes, renal function, liver function tests, albumin, calcium, urinalysis, lactate dehydrogenase, CRP.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: What is the clinical significance of identifying EGFR mutations in the molecular profiling of lung cancer?
back: Identifying activating EGFR mutations predicts a positive response to EGFR inhibitor targeted therapies (e.g., gefitinib, erlotinib, or osimertinib).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 137 (Book Page): EGFR mutations – predict response to EGFR inhibitor targeted therapy in lung cancer.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Which three non-ovarian malignancies are commonly associated with an elevated serum CA-125 tumour marker?
back: 1. Gastrointestinal cancer (10%); 2. Lung cancer (5%); 3. Breast cancer (5%). It also rises in any cause of ascites or heart failure.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 136 (Book Page): Cancer antigen 125 (CA-125)... Raised in any cause of ascites, pleural effusion or heart failure... Ovarian epithelial cancer (75%), gastrointestinal cancer (10%), lung cancer (5%) and breast cancer (5%).

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Beyond the ECOG scale, which biochemical findings indicate a worse prognosis when assessing patient fitness?
back: 1. Low serum albumin levels. 2. Raised inflammatory markers (increased white blood cell count and C-reactive protein).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 137 (Book Page): Outcomes for patients with PS 3–4 are worse in almost all malignancies than for those with PS 0–2... Additionally, outcomes are typically worse for patients with a low albumin and raised inflammatory markers (i.e. white blood cell count, C-reactive protein).

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: During histological investigation of metastatic tissue, which microscopic finding strongly suggests a gastric primary?
back: The presence of signet-ring cells on light microscopy strongly favours a gastric origin for the malignancy.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 136 (Book Page): Examination of tumour samples by light microscopy remains the core method of cancer diagnosis and... Signet-ring cells favour a gastric primary.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: What is the essential difference between cytologic and histopathologic investigation in cancer diagnosis?
back: Cytology examines individual cells (fluids/FNA); histopathology examines tissue samples to identify tumour architecture, providing information to direct management.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 135 (Book Page): At times a diagnosis can be obtained by examination of cells (cytology) from fluid... [Page 136 (Book Page)] Histopathological analysis of tumour tissue is pivotal in identifying the type of cancer and provides information that may direct subsequent management.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: What is the investigation of choice to confirm and differentiate the causes of SVCO?
back: A CT scan of the thorax is the investigation of choice to distinguish between extrinsic compression and intravascular causes.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 141 (Book Page): The investigation of choice is a CT scan of the thorax to confirm the diagnosis and distinguish between extra- and intravascular causes.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Which imaging modality is considered the standard for staging cancers of the thorax and abdomen?
back: Computed Tomography (CT).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Computed tomography (CT) is a key investigation in cancer patients and is particularly useful in imaging the thorax and abdomen

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: What is the biological basis for using PET-CT in the assessment of distant metastases?
back: It visualises the metabolic activity of tumour cells, helping evaluate the extent of disease before radical treatment.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Positron emission tomography (PET) visualises metabolic activity of tumour cells and is often used in combination with CT (PET–CT) to evaluate the extent of the disease

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Contrast the specific diagnostic roles of MRI versus CT in oncological staging.
back: MRI is preferred for high-resolution imaging of the brain, bone, and pelvis (e.g., rectal or prostate cancers); CT is used for thorax and abdomen.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has a high resolution and is the preferred technique for brain, bone and pelvic imaging. It is widely employed for the staging of rectal, cervical and prostate cancers.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: A patient presents with a palpable neck lump. List the core steps in performing a fine needle aspiration (FNA).
back:
- Immobilise the lesion.
- Apply negative pressure using a syringe.
- Make multiple rapid passes at various angles.
- Expel material onto a glass slide.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): Box 7.5: Immobilise the lesion... Apply negative pressure by pulling on the syringe... Make multiple rapid passes through the lesion... Withdraw the needle and expel the cellular material... onto the labelled glass slide

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: How does immunohistochemistry (IHC) for ER, PR, and HER2 influence the management of breast cancer?
back: ER/PR positivity indicates sensitivity to hormonal manipulation; HER2 positivity indicates response to HER2 inhibitors (e.g., trastuzumab).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): Oestrogen (ER) and progesterone (PR) receptor positivity indicate that the cancer may be sensitive to hormonal manipulation... HER2 receptor positivity in breast or gastric cancers indicate that the tumour may respond to HER2 inhibitor targeted therapy.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Define the components of the UICC T, N, and M staging classification.
back:
- T: Size/extent of primary tumour.
- N: Regional lymph node involvement.
- M: Presence of distant metastases.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 163 (Book Page): Box 7.3: T (tumour), N (regional lymph nodes), M (metastatic sites) approach of the International Union against Cancer

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Which serum tumour markers are essential for the diagnosis and monitoring of germ-cell tumours?
back: Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG) favour germ-cell tumours.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Why is a biopsy mandatory for a single lytic bone lesion even if imaging suggests metastasis?
back: Primary bone tumours can mimic the radiological appearance of metastases; tissue diagnosis prevents management errors.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 172 (Book Page): In patients with a single lesion, it is especially important to perform a biopsy to obtain a tissue diagnosis, since primary bone tumours may look very similar to metastases on X-ray.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Why must CA-125 be interpreted cautiously in the diagnosis of ovarian cancer?
back: It is non-specific; levels rise in any cause of ascites, pleural effusion, heart failure, or inflammatory conditions.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 164 (Book Page): Box 7.4: [CA-125] Raised in any cause of ascites, pleural effusion or heart failure. Can be raised in inflammatory conditions

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: How do ALK and EGFR molecular profiling investigations direct management in lung cancer?
back: EGFR mutations predict response to EGFR inhibitors (e.g., gefitinib); ALK rearrangements predict response to ALK inhibitors.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): EGFR mutations – predict response to EGFR inhibitor... ALK fusion oncogene rearrangement – predict response to ALK inhibitor

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: What are the three core components of the UICC TNM system for cancer staging?
back:
- T: Size/extent of primary tumour
- N: Involvement of regional lymph nodes
- M: Presence of distant metastases
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): One of the most commonly used systems is the T (tumour), N (regional lymph nodes), M (metastatic sites) approach of the International Union against Cancer (UICC).

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Explain the diagnostic role of Positron Emission Tomography (PET) in cancer management.
back:
- Visualises metabolic activity of tumour cells
- Often combined with CT (PET-CT)
- Evaluates disease extent and distant metastases for radical treatment planning
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Positron emission tomography (PET) visualises metabolic activity of tumour cells and is often used in combination with CT (PET–CT) to evaluate the extent of the disease, particularly in the assessment of potential distant metastases.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Contrast the primary anatomical indications for CT versus MRI in oncological staging.
back:
- CT: Best for thorax and abdomen imaging
- MRI: Preferred for brain, bone, and pelvic imaging (rectal, cervical, prostate)
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): [CT] is particularly useful in imaging the thorax and abdomen... [MRI] has a high resolution and is the preferred technique for brain, bone and pelvic imaging.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Which investigation is prioritized for determining cancer type in a patient with metastatic disease of unknown primary?
back:
- Core biopsy of the most accessible metastatic lesion
- Followed by histopathology, immunohistochemistry (IHC), and molecular pathology
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 167 (Book Page): ...a core biopsy of the most accessible metastatic lesion is usually the quickest way of obtaining tissue for pathological evaluation of cancer type. Review of tumour morphology, immunohistochemistry and molecular pathology will usually be sufficient.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: How does immunohistochemistry (IHC) staining for HER2 receptors guide pharmacological management in breast cancer?
back:
- Detects HER2 receptor over-expression
- Positive results indicate potential response to HER2 inhibitor targeted therapy (e.g., Trastuzumab)
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): HER2 receptor positivity in breast or gastric cancers indicate that the tumour may respond to HER2 inhibitor targeted therapy.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Define the clinical utility of the ECOG scale in cancer management.
back:
- Performance Status (PS) scale (0–4)
- Formally assesses patient fitness
- Directs management; patients with PS 3–4 have poorer outcomes and limited treatment options
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): The Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status (PS) scale is used to formally assess a patient’s fitness... Outcomes for patients with PS 3–4 are worse in almost all malignancies.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Why are serum tumour markers like CA-125 generally avoided as standalone diagnostic tools?
back:
- Lacks sufficient sensitivity and specificity
- Can be elevated in benign/inflammatory conditions (e.g., heart failure, ascites, or cirrhosis)
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 163 (Book Page): Unfortunately, most tumour markers are neither sufficiently sensitive nor sufficiently specific to be used in isolation for diagnosis and need to be interpreted in the context of other clinical features.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: In histopathology, which microscopic findings suggest a gastric versus an ovarian primary cancer?
back:
- Gastric: Signet-ring cells
- Ovarian: Psammoma bodies and mucin-positive staining
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 164 (Book Page)-165: Signet-ring cells favour a gastric primary... Psammoma bodies are a feature of ovarian cancer (mucin +) and thyroid cancer (mucin -).

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Explain the role of RAS mutation molecular testing in colorectal cancer management.
back:
- Identifies resistance to EGFR inhibitor targeted therapy (e.g., Cetuximab)
- Essential to test before initiating EGFR-targeted treatment
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): RAS mutations – predict resistance to EGFR inhibitor targeted therapy in colon cancer.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: What are the standardized RECIST categories used to evaluate cancer treatment response?
back:
- Complete Response (CR): Disappearance of target lesions
- Partial Response (PR): ≥30% decrease in lesion diameter
- Progressive Disease (PD): ≥20% increase or new lesions
- Stable Disease (SD)
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 176 (Book Page): Uniform criteria have been established... response evaluation criteria in solid tumours (RECIST, Box 7.19).

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: What three core components must be established through investigations to plan a cancer patient's management?
back:
1. Extent of disease (staging).
2. Specific type of cancer (histopathology).
3. Patient's fitness for treatment (ECOG Performance Status).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): 'In order to plan the most appropriate investigations and management, information is needed on: the extent of disease, the type of cancer, the patient’s fitness.'

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: On light microscopy, which cellular features suggest a gastric primary versus an ovarian or thyroid primary?
back:
• Gastric: Presence of Signet-ring cells.
• Ovarian/Thyroid: Presence of Psammoma bodies (Ovarian is mucin positive; thyroid is mucin negative).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 164 (Book Page): 'Signet-ring cells favour a gastric primary... Psammoma bodies are a feature of ovarian cancer (mucin +) and thyroid cancer (mucin -).'

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Which anatomical regions and specific cancers are prioritized for MRI over CT during staging?
back:
• Regions: Brain, bone, and pelvis.
• Cancers: Rectal, cervical, and prostate cancers due to high resolution in these areas.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): 'Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)... is the preferred technique for brain, bone and pelvic imaging. It is widely employed for the staging of rectal, cervical and prostate cancers.'

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: During Fine Needle Aspiration (FNA), what specific observation necessitates immediate cessation of the sampling procedure?
back: The presence of blood in the syringe hub. Blood contamination reduces the diagnostic quality of the cellular sample.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): 'Stop sampling if blood is seen in the syringe hub as blood reduces the quality of the sample.'

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: How do RAS and EGFR mutations respectively influence the use of EGFR inhibitors in colon and lung cancer?
back:
• EGFR mutations: Predict positive response to inhibitors in lung cancer.
• RAS mutations: Predict resistance to EGFR inhibitors in colon cancer.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): 'EGFR mutations – predict response to EGFR inhibitor targeted therapy in lung cancer; RAS mutations – predict resistance to EGFR inhibitor targeted therapy in colon cancer.'

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Which two serum tumour markers are essential for diagnosing and monitoring non-seminomatous germ cell tumours?
back:
1. Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP): Elevated in 80%.
2. Human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG): Elevated in 50%–80%.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 164 (Book Page): 'Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP)... Ovarian non-seminomatous germ cell tumours (80%), testicular teratoma (80%)... Human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG)... (50%–80%)'

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Why might PET-CT fail to detect malignancy in certain patients despite active disease?
back:
1. Some tumour types are not 'PET-avid' (low metabolic activity).
2. The system has limited sensitivity for detecting very small (though malignant) lymph nodes.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): 'Not all tumour types are ‘PET-avid’ and the metabolic activity of small but malignant lymph nodes may not be detected, limiting the sensitivity of PET-CT.'

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: When is extensive staging and diagnostic investigation clinically discouraged in a suspected cancer patient?
back: When a patient has a poor ECOG Performance Status (3–4) or comorbidities that preclude treatment. In these cases, investigations add little clinical value.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): 'In some patients poor fitness or comorbidities may preclude any anti-cancer therapy options, in which case comprehensive diagnostic and staging investigations add little clinical value'

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: What clinical significance is assigned to oestrogen receptor (ER) and progesterone receptor (PR) positivity in cancer biopsy samples?
back: Positivity indicates that the cancer (typically breast) may be sensitive to and responsive to hormonal manipulation therapy.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): 'Oestrogen (ER) and progesterone (PR) receptor positivity indicate that the cancer may be sensitive to hormonal manipulation.'

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Which cytogenetic translocation is specific for diagnosing Ewing's sarcoma via FISH analysis?
back: The translocation between chromosome 11 and 22: t(11;22)(q24;q12).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): 'fluorescent in situ hybridisation (FISH) techniques can be useful in Ewing's sarcoma... where there is a translocation between chromosome 11 and 22: t(11;22)(q24;q12).'

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
coreConcept: Tumour Markers for Germ Cell Malignancy
front: Q: Which two serum tumour markers are essential for diagnosing and monitoring non-seminomatous germ cell tumours?
back:
• Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP)
• Human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG)
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 164 (Book Page): [Commonly used serum tumour markers] Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP)... Ovarian non-seminomatous germ cell tumours (80%), testicular teratoma (80%)... Human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG)... Choriocarcinoma (100%), hydatidiform moles (97%), ovarian non-seminomatous germ cell tumours (50%–80%)

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: What is the physiological basis and primary utility of Positron Emission Tomography (PET) in cancer staging?
back:
• Visualises metabolic activity of tumour cells.
• Primarily used to evaluate distant metastases before radical treatment.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): [Positron emission tomography] Positron emission tomography (PET) visualises metabolic activity of tumour cells and is often used in combination with CT (PET–CT) to evaluate the extent of the disease, particularly in the assessment of potential distant metastases when a radical treatment approach is being considered.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Contrast the preferred imaging modalities for staging the thorax/abdomen versus the brain/pelvis.
back:
• Thorax/Abdomen: Computed Tomography (CT).
• Brain/Bone/Pelvis: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): [Computed tomography] Computed tomography (CT) is a key investigation in cancer patients and is particularly useful in imaging the thorax and abdomen... [Magnetic resonance imaging] Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has a high resolution and is the preferred technique for brain, bone and pelvic imaging.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: What is the definitive imaging investigation required for a patient suspected of malignant spinal cord compression?
back: • Urgent MRI scan of the whole spine.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 168 (Book Page): [Management of suspected spinal cord compression] Confirm diagnosis with urgent MRI scan of whole spine.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: How do Immunohistochemistry (IHC) markers ER, PR, and HER2 influence breast cancer management?
back:
• ER/PR positivity: Predicts sensitivity to hormonal manipulation.
• HER2 positivity: Predicts response to HER2 inhibitor targeted therapy (e.g., Trastuzumab).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): [Immunohistochemistry] Oestrogen (ER) and progesterone (PR) receptor positivity indicate that the cancer may be sensitive to hormonal manipulation... HER2 receptor positivity in breast or gastric cancers indicate that the tumour may respond to HER2 inhibitor targeted therapy.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Define ECOG Performance Status Grade 2 and its significance in treatment planning.
back:
• Patient is ambulatory, capable of all self-care, but unable to work; up >50% of waking hours.
• Determines if the patient is fit for aggressive anti-cancer therapy.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): [ECOG performance status scale] 2: Ambulatory and capable of all self-care but unable to work. Up and about more than 50% of waking hours.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: What diagnostic role does molecular pathology play in selecting therapy for lung adenocarcinoma?
back:
• Identifies EGFR mutations or ALK fusion rearrangements.
• Predicts response to specific tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): [Molecular pathology] EGFR mutations – predict response to EGFR inhibitor targeted therapy in lung cancer... ALK fusion oncogene rearrangement – predict response to ALK inhibitor targeted therapy in lung cancer.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: In Cancer of Unknown Primary (CUP), which initial investigation is prioritized to establish the tissue diagnosis?
back: • Core biopsy of the most accessible metastatic lesion for histopathology and IHC.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 167 (Book Page): [Metastatic malignant disease of undefined primary origin] If patients are fit... a core biopsy of the most accessible metastatic lesion is usually the quickest way of obtaining tissue for pathological evaluation of cancer type.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Which pre-treatment biochemical marker correlates with tumour bulk and predicts risk for Tumour Lysis Syndrome?
back: • Serum Lactate Dehydrogenase (LDH).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 170 (Book Page): [Tumour lysis syndrome] Elevated serum potassium may be the earliest biochemical marker but pre-treatment serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) correlates with tumour bulk and may indicate increased risk.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Identify the primary cancer site suggested by 'Signet-ring cells' and 'Psammoma bodies' on light microscopy.
back:
• Signet-ring cells: Gastric primary.
• Psammoma bodies: Ovarian or Thyroid cancer.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 164 (Book Page): [Light microscopy] Signet-ring cells favour a gastric primary... Psammoma bodies are a feature of ovarian cancer (mucin +) and thyroid cancer (mucin -).

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Which serum tumour marker is most specific for screening hepatocellular carcinoma and non-seminomatous germ cell tumours?
back: Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 164 (Book Page): [Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP)] Ovarian non-seminomatous germ cell tumours (80%), testicular teratoma (80%), hepatocellular cancer (50%)

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: What is the primary functional role of Positron Emission Tomography (PET) in cancer staging?
back: It visualises the metabolic activity of tumour cells to evaluate disease extent and distant metastases.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Positron emission tomography (PET) visualises metabolic activity of tumour cells and is often used in combination with CT (PET–CT) to evaluate the extent of the disease

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Contrast the preferred clinical uses of CT vs. MRI in oncological imaging.
back:
• CT: Thorax and abdomen.
• MRI: High-resolution for brain, bone, and pelvic (rectal/prostate) imaging.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Computed tomography (CT) is... particularly useful in imaging the thorax and abdomen... Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)... is the preferred technique for brain, bone and pelvic imaging.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: How does a detected RAS mutation impact the management of colorectal cancer?
back: It predicts resistance to EGFR inhibitor targeted therapy (e.g., cetuximab), making these drugs ineffective.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): RAS mutations – predict resistance to EGFR inhibitor targeted therapy in colon cancer

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: What is the clinical significance of testing for HER2 receptor positivity in breast or gastric cancers?
back: It indicates the tumour may respond to HER2-inhibitor targeted therapy (e.g., Trastuzumab).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): HER2 receptor positivity in breast or gastric cancers indicate that the tumour may respond to HER2 inhibitor targeted therapy.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: List the three essential categories of information required to plan cancer management.
back:
1. Extent of disease (Staging).
2. Type of cancer (Histopathology).
3. Patient’s fitness (Performance Status).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): In order to plan the most appropriate investigations and management, information is needed on: the extent of disease, the type of cancer, the patient’s fitness.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: How do serum albumin and inflammatory markers assist in assessing a cancer patient's fitness?
back: Low albumin and raised inflammatory markers (CRP, WBC) signify poor prognosis and may preclude aggressive therapy.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): outcomes are typically worse for patients with a low albumin and raised inflammatory markers (i.e. white blood cell count, C-reactive protein).

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: On light microscopy, the presence of 'signet-ring cells' indicates which primary cancer site?
back: Gastric (Stomach) primary.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 164 (Book Page): Signet-ring cells favour a gastric primary.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Define ECOG Performance Status 3 and its impact on clinical decision-making.
back:
• Definition: Confined to bed/chair >50% of waking hours; limited self-care.
• Impact: Poor prognosis; aggressive treatment is often inappropriate.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): 3: Capable of only limited self-care, confined to bed or chair more than 50% of waking hours... Outcomes for patients with PS 3–4 are worse

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: What cytogenetic finding is diagnostic for Ewing's sarcoma using FISH analysis?
back: Translocation between chromosome 11 and 22: t(11;22)(q24;q12).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): FISH techniques can be useful in Ewing's sarcoma... where there is a translocation between chromosome 11 and 22: t(11;22)(q24;q12).

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Which three serum tumor markers are primarily used in the investigation of suspected germ-cell tumors?
back:
• Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP)
• Human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG)
• Placental alkaline phosphatase (PLAP)
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 164 (Book Page): [Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP)... Ovarian non-seminomatous germ cell tumours (80%), testicular teratoma (80%)... hCG... ovarian non-seminomatous germ cell tumours (50%–80%)... PLAP... Seminoma (40%)]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: What is the specific diagnostic role of Positron Emission Tomography (PET-CT) in cancer staging?
back:
• Visualizes metabolic activity of tumor cells
• Evaluates extent of disease
• Assesses distant metastases when planning radical treatment
