citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): [PET visualises metabolic activity of tumour cells... evaluate the extent of the disease, particularly in the assessment of potential distant metastases when a radical treatment approach is being considered.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Which two cancers are identified microscopically by the presence of Psammoma bodies?
back:
• Ovarian cancer (mucin positive)
• Thyroid cancer (mucin negative)
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): [Psammoma bodies are a feature of ovarian cancer (mucin +) and thyroid cancer (mucin -).]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Define ECOG Performance Status Grade 3 and its impact on management decisions.
back:
• Definition: Capable of only limited self-care; bed/chair >50% of waking hours
• Management: Poorer prognosis; aggressive anti-cancer therapy is often precluded
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): [3: Capable of only limited self-care, confined to bed or chair more than 50% of waking hours... In some patients poor fitness or comorbidities may preclude any anti-cancer therapy options.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: How does identifying a RAS mutation via molecular pathology alter colon cancer management?
back:
• Predicts resistance to EGFR inhibitor targeted therapy (e.g., cetuximab)
• Prevents the use of ineffective, expensive targeted treatments
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): [RAS mutations – predict resistance to EGFR inhibitor targeted therapy in colon cancer.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Which imaging modality is preferred for staging brain, bone, and pelvic malignancies (rectal/prostate)?
back:
• Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI)
• Preferred due to superior resolution for pelvic and soft tissue anatomy
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): [MRI... is the preferred technique for brain, bone and pelvic imaging. It is widely employed for the staging of rectal, cervical and prostate cancers.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: According to RECIST criteria, what constitutes a 'Partial Response' (PR) to treatment?
back:
• At least a 30% decrease in the sum of the longest diameter (LD) of target lesions
• Uses baseline sum LD as the reference
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 176 (Book Page): [Partial response (PR): At least a 30% decrease in the sum of the longest diameter (LD) of target lesions, taking as reference the baseline sum LD.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: During Fine Needle Aspiration (FNA), why must the operator stop if blood appears in the syringe?
back:
• Blood presence reduces the diagnostic quality of the cellular sample
• Obscures malignant cells during pathological evaluation
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): [Stop sampling if blood is seen in the syringe hub as blood reduces the quality of the sample.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: List three diagnostic roles of ultrasound in the management of cancer patients.
back:
• Characterizing lesions (liver, kidney, pancreas)
• Guiding needle biopsies (breast, liver)
• Staging upper GI cancers (Endoscopic Ultrasound)
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): [Ultrasound is useful in characterising lesions... It may be used for guiding biopsies... Endoscopic ultrasound is helpful in staging upper gastrointestinal and pancreatic cancers.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: What are the clinical limitations of CA-125 as a diagnostic marker for ovarian cancer?
back:
• Poor specificity
• Elevated in non-malignant causes: ascites, pleural effusion, heart failure, and inflammation
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 164 (Book Page): [CA-125... Raised in any cause of ascites, pleural effusion or heart failure. Can be raised in inflammatory conditions.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: What are the three components of the International Union against Cancer (UICC) TNM staging system?
back:
* T: Size or depth of primary tumour
* N: Regional lymph node involvement
* M: Presence of distant metastases
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): One of the most commonly used systems is the T (tumour), N (regional lymph nodes), M (metastatic sites) approach of the International Union against Cancer (UICC, see Box 7.3).

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: What is the primary physiological mechanism utilized by PET scans to visualize cancer?
back: PET visualises the metabolic activity of tumour cells, often combined with CT (PET-CT) to evaluate the extent of distant metastases.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Positron emission tomography (PET) visualises metabolic activity of tumour cells and is often used in combination with CT (PET–CT) to evaluate the extent of the disease.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Contrast the preferred clinical use of MRI versus CT in oncological imaging.
back:
* MRI: High resolution for brain, bone, and pelvic (rectal/prostate) imaging.
* CT: Preferred for imaging the thorax and abdomen.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): Computed tomography (CT) is... particularly useful in imaging the thorax and abdomen. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has a high resolution and is the preferred technique for brain, bone and pelvic imaging.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Why might a bone scan be falsely negative in a patient with Multiple Myeloma?
back: Isotope bone scans depend on osteoblastic activity; myeloma involves suppression of osteoblasts, making plain X-rays or MRI the preferred investigation.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 172 (Book Page): [Isotope bone scan] false-negative results occur in multiple myeloma due to suppression of osteoblast activity. Plain X-ray films or MRI scans are therefore preferred.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: What is the clinical significance of testing for EGFR and ALK mutations in lung cancer?
back: They serve as predictive biomarkers for 'druggable' pathways: EGFR mutations predict response to EGFR inhibitors; ALK fusions predict response to ALK inhibitors.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): EGFR mutations – predict response to EGFR inhibitor targeted therapy in lung cancer... ALK fusion oncogene rearrangement – predict response to ALK inhibitor targeted therapy in lung cancer.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Which serum tumour markers are essential for diagnosing and monitoring non-seminomatous germ cell tumours (NSGCT)?
back:
* Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP)
* Human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG)
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 164 (Book Page): Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP)... Ovarian non-seminomatous germ cell tumours (80%), testicular teratoma (80%)... Human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG)... Ovarian non-seminomatous germ cell tumours (50%–80%).

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Define 'Partial Response' (PR) in cancer management based on RECIST criteria.
back: At least a 30% decrease in the sum of the longest diameters of target lesions, using the baseline sum as reference.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 176 (Book Page): Partial response (PR): At least a 30% decrease in the sum of the longest diameter (LD) of target lesions, taking as reference the baseline sum LD.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: A patient with an unknown primary has signet-ring cells on biopsy. What is the likely origin?
back: Signet-ring cells strongly favor a gastric (stomach) primary cancer.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 164 (Book Page): Light microscopy... Signet-ring cells favour a gastric primary.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Why must serum calcium be adjusted for albumin when investigating suspected malignancy-associated hypercalcaemia?
back: Total calcium under-estimates the physiologically active ionised calcium levels because hypoalbuminaemia is common in cancer patients.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 170 (Book Page): It is especially important to correct for albumin in cancer because hypoalbuminaemia is common and total calcium values under-estimate the level of ionised calcium.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: What does ECOG Performance Status Grade 3 signify regarding a patient's fitness for treatment?
back: The patient is capable of only limited self-care and is confined to a bed or chair for more than 50% of waking hours.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): ECOG performance status scale... 3: Capable of only limited self-care, confined to bed or chair more than 50% of waking hours.

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: What scale is used to formally assess a cancer patient’s fitness for treatment?
back: Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status. Scores range from 0 (fully active) to 4 (completely disabled). Scores 3-4 suggest worse outcomes.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): [The Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status (PS) scale is used to formally assess a patient’s fitness (Box 7.6).]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Why is PET-CT specifically utilized during radical cancer treatment planning?
back: It visualizes metabolic activity. It is used to evaluate disease extent and detect distant metastases when radical treatment is considered.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): [Positron emission tomography (PET) visualizes metabolic activity of tumour cells and is often used in combination with CT (PET–CT) to evaluate the extent of the disease, particularly in the assessment of potential distant metastases when a radical treatment approach is being considered.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Differentiate the primary imaging utility of CT versus MRI in oncology.
back: CT is preferred for thorax and abdomen imaging. MRI has higher resolution for brain, bone, and pelvic (rectal, cervical, prostate) staging.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): [Computed tomography (CT) is... particularly useful in imaging the thorax and abdomen. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has a high resolution and is the preferred technique for brain, bone and pelvic imaging.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: A young man presents with a bulky midline mass. Which investigations are prioritized?
back: Serum Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG). These markers are highly suggestive of germ-cell tumours requiring urgent therapy.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 167 (Book Page): [Tumour markers: ...α-fetoprotein (AFP) and human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG) in midline disease in young men... suggestive of a non-seminomatous testicular cancer.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: What is the clinical significance of testing for RAS mutations in colorectal cancer?
back: RAS mutations predict resistance to EGFR inhibitor targeted therapy (e.g., cetuximab). Testing identifies patients who will not benefit from these agents.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): [RAS mutations – predict resistance to EGFR inhibitor targeted therapy in colon cancer.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Define 'Partial Response' in cancer management according to RECIST criteria.
back: A minimum 30% decrease in the sum of the longest diameters (LD) of target lesions, using the baseline sum as a reference.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 176 (Book Page): [Partial response (PR): At least a 30% decrease in the sum of the longest diameter (LD) of target lesions, taking as reference the baseline sum LD.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Which non-malignant conditions can cause a false-positive rise in CA-125?
back: Any cause of ascites, pleural effusion, heart failure, or various inflammatory conditions. It lacks high specificity for ovarian cancer diagnosis in isolation.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 164 (Book Page): [Cancer antigen 125 (CA-125)... Raised in any cause of ascites, pleural effusion or heart failure. Can be raised in inflammatory conditions.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Under light microscopy, what do signet-ring cells and Psammoma bodies suggest?
back: Signet-ring cells favor a gastric primary. Psammoma bodies are characteristic of ovarian cancer (mucin positive) or thyroid cancer (mucin negative).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 164 (Book Page)-165: [Signet-ring cells favour a gastric primary... Psammoma bodies are a feature of ovarian cancer (mucin +) and thyroid cancer (mucin -).]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Which biochemical marker serves as the best indicator of high-risk Tumour Lysis Syndrome?
back: Serum Lactate Dehydrogenase (LDH). High pre-treatment levels correlate with large tumour bulk and increased risk of metabolic collapse.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 170 (Book Page): [Pre-treatment serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) correlates with tumour bulk and may indicate increased risk (of Tumour Lysis Syndrome).]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: What is the mandatory investigation to confirm a specific tumour type?
back: Histopathological analysis of tissue obtained via biopsy (core, excision, or endoscopic). It remains the gold standard for identifying the cancer type.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 164 (Book Page): [Histopathological analysis of tumour tissue is pivotal in identifying the type of cancer and provides information that may direct subsequent management.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: What are the three essential categories of information required to plan cancer investigations and management?
back:
• Extent of disease (staging)
• Type of cancer (histopathology)
• Patient’s fitness (performance status)
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): [In order to plan the most appropriate investigations and management, information is needed on: • the extent of disease • the type of cancer • the patient’s fitness.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: How does Positron Emission Tomography (PET) facilitate the staging of radical treatment candidates?
back:
• Visualises the metabolic activity of tumour cells
• Combined with CT (PET-CT) to assess distant metastases
• Critical for determining eligibility for radical therapy
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): [Positron emission tomography (PET) visualises metabolic activity of tumour cells and is often used in combination with CT (PET–CT) to evaluate the extent of the disease, particularly in the assessment of potential distant metastases when a radical treatment approach is being considered.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Contrast the preferred imaging modalities for thoracic/abdominal staging versus brain/pelvic staging.
back:
• Thorax/Abdomen: Computed Tomography (CT) is the key investigation
• Brain/Pelvis: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is preferred for higher resolution
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): [Computed tomography (CT) is a key investigation... particularly useful in imaging the thorax and abdomen. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has a high resolution and is the preferred technique for brain, bone and pelvic imaging.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
coreConcept: Biochemical Markers in Germ Cell Tumours
front: In a young male with a midline tumour, which biochemical markers must be measured urgently?
back:
• Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP)
• Human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG)
• Essential to identify highly treatable germ cell tumours
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 167 (Book Page): [Tumour markers... α-fetoprotein (AFP) and human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG) in midline disease in young men... suggestive of a non-seminomatous testicular cancer.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: How does Immunohistochemistry (IHC) for HER2 receptors determine the pharmacological strategy in breast cancer?
back:
• Confirms HER2 receptor over-expression
• Predicts response to targeted therapies
• Directs the use of HER2 inhibitors like Trastuzumab
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): [HER2 receptor positivity in breast or gastric cancers indicate that the tumour may respond to HER2 inhibitor targeted therapy.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: What is the RECIST criterion for defining a 'Partial Response' (PR) to treatment?
back:
• Minimum 30% decrease in the sum of longest diameters (LD)
• Reference is the baseline sum of LD of target lesions
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 176 (Book Page): [Partial response (PR): At least a 30% decrease in the sum of the longest diameter (LD) of target lesions, taking as reference the baseline sum LD]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: How does an ECOG Performance Status of 3-4 influence the decision to pursue staging investigations?
back:
• Indicates poor fitness and high mortality risk
• Aggressive anti-cancer therapy is often precluded
• Extensive staging adds little value if treatment is not feasible
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): [Outcomes for patients with PS 3–4 are worse... In some patients poor fitness or comorbidities may preclude any anti-cancer therapy options, in which case comprehensive diagnostic and staging investigations add little clinical value.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Why might an isotope bone scan provide a misleading 'flare response' during cancer management?
back:
• Healing bone following treatment shows increased tracer uptake
• Represents a false-positive for progression
• MRI or plain X-rays are required for confirmation
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 172 (Book Page): [Isotope bone scan... can have false-positive results in healing bone, particularly as a flare response following treatment.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Why is the Serum Total Calcium measurement alone insufficient in the investigation of malignant hypercalcaemia?
back:
• Hypoalbuminaemia is common in cancer patients
• Total calcium underestimates ionised (active) calcium
• Adjustment for albumin is mandatory for accurate diagnosis
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 170 (Book Page): [The diagnosis is made by measuring serum total calcium and adjusting for albumin. It is especially important to correct for albumin in cancer because hypoalbuminaemia is common and total calcium values under-estimate the level of ionised calcium.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: What investigation is diagnostic for Superior Vena Cava Obstruction (SVCO)?
back:
• CT scan of the thorax
• Confirms diagnosis and distinguishes extrinsic compression from intravascular causes
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 169 (Book Page): [The investigation of choice is a CT scan of the thorax to confirm the diagnosis and distinguish between extra- and intravascular causes.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Define the primary components of the TNM staging system used in cancer investigations.
back:
• T: Extent of primary tumour
• N: Presence/extent of regional lymph node involvement
• M: Presence of distant metastatic sites
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 133 (Book Page): [The outcome is recorded using a standard staging classification... One of the most commonly used systems is the T (tumour), N (regional lymph nodes), M (metastatic sites) approach.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: What is the primary role of Positron Emission Tomography (PET-CT) in cancer management?
back:
• Visualises metabolic activity of tumour cells
• Evaluates disease extent/distant metastases
• Critical when considering radical (curative) treatment approaches
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 134 (Book Page): [PET visualises metabolic activity of tumour cells and is often used in combination with CT (PET–CT) to evaluate the extent of the disease, particularly in the assessment of potential distant metastases when a radical treatment approach is being considered.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: For which specific anatomical sites is MRI the preferred staging investigation over CT?
back:
• Brain
• Bone
• Pelvis (specifically rectal, cervical, and prostate cancers)
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 134 (Book Page): [Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has a high resolution and is the preferred technique for brain, bone and pelvic imaging. It is widely employed for the staging of rectal, cervical and prostate cancers.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: How does a patient's ECOG Performance Status (PS) Grade 3 influence clinical management?
back:
• Indicates limited self-care; confined to bed/chair >50% of waking hours
• Associated with worse outcomes
• May preclude aggressive anti-cancer therapy
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 137 (Book Page): [Outcomes for patients with PS 3–4 are worse in almost all malignancies than for those with PS 0–2... poor fitness or comorbidities may preclude any anti-cancer therapy options.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Which Immunohistochemical (IHC) markers predict sensitivity to hormonal manipulation in breast cancer?
back:
• Oestrogen Receptor (ER) positivity
• Progesterone Receptor (PR) positivity
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 137 (Book Page): [Oestrogen (ER) and progesterone (PR) receptor positivity indicate that the cancer may be sensitive to hormonal manipulation.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Name the specific serum tumour marker used to screen for Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia (MEN) 2.
back: • Calcitonin (produced by C-cells of the thyroid)
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 136 (Book Page): [Calcitonin: 32-amino-acid peptide from C cells of thyroid. Used to screen for MEN 2. Medullary cell carcinoma of thyroid.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: What is the clinical significance of detecting 'microsatellite instability' via molecular profiling?
back: • Predicts therapeutic response to checkpoint inhibitor immunotherapy across several cancer types.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 137 (Book Page): [microsatellite instability – predict response to checkpoint inhibitor immunotherapy in several cancer types]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: What is the gold-standard urgent investigation for a patient with suspected Malignant Spinal Cord Compression?
back: • Urgent MRI scan of the whole spine (to identify vertebral masses or intrathecal metastases).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 140 (Book Page): [Confirm diagnosis with urgent MRI scan of whole spine]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Which biochemical markers define the metabolic sequelae of Tumour Lysis Syndrome (TLS)?
back:
• Hyperkalaemia
• Hyperphosphataemia
• Hyperuricaemia
• Hypocalcaemia (transient)
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 142 (Book Page): [Cellular destruction results in the release of potassium, phosphate, nucleic acids and purines that can cause transient hypocalcaemia, hyperphosphataemia, hyperuricaemia and hyperkalaemia.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: In cancer investigations, what does the finding of a 'Sister Mary Joseph Nodule' indicate?
back: • Umbilical nodule representing metastatic spread, typically from intra-abdominal malignancies (e.g., ovarian or gastric carcinoma).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 150 (Book Page): [Occasionally, peritoneal deposits are palpable as an omental ‘cake’ and nodules in the umbilicus (Sister Mary Joseph nodules).]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: What three fundamental categories of information are required to plan an appropriate cancer management plan?
back:
1. Extent of disease (Staging)
2. Type of cancer (Histology/Pathology)
3. Patient's fitness (Performance Status)
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 161 (Book Page): [In order to plan the most appropriate investigations and management, information is needed on: the extent of disease, the type of cancer, the patient’s fitness.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Contrast the primary imaging roles of CT versus MRI in oncological staging.
back:
• CT: Best for thorax and abdomen (e.g., CT colonography).
• MRI: Preferred for brain, bone, and pelvic imaging (rectal, cervical, prostate).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page): [Computed tomography (CT) is... particularly useful in imaging the thorax and abdomen... Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)... is the preferred technique for brain, bone and pelvic imaging.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: How does the presence of RAS mutations influence the management of colon cancer?
back: RAS mutations predict resistance to EGFR inhibitor targeted therapy (e.g., cetuximab, panitumumab), guiding against their use.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): [RAS mutations – predict resistance to EGFR inhibitor targeted therapy in colon cancer]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Match microscopic features: Signet-ring cells, Melanin, and Psammoma bodies to their most likely cancer origins.
back:
• Signet-ring cells: Gastric
• Melanin: Melanoma
• Psammoma bodies: Ovarian or Thyroid
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 164 (Book Page)-165: [Signet-ring cells favour a gastric primary. Presence of melanin favours melanoma... Psammoma bodies are a feature of ovarian cancer (mucin + ) and thyroid cancer (mucin - )]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Define the clinical criteria for ECOG Performance Status (PS) Grade 3.
back: Capable of limited self-care only; confined to bed or chair more than 50% of waking hours.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): [Grade 3: Capable of only limited self-care, confined to bed or chair more than 50% of waking hours]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: A patient with suspected metastatic cancer presents with low albumin and high CRP. What is the clinical implication?
back: Indicates poor prognosis irrespective of diagnosis; aggressive investigations may be clinical value-limited, favoring palliative focus.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 167 (Book Page): [Features associated with poor prognosis... poor performance status (PS 3–4)... raised inflammatory markers and low albumin. Further investigations... may not be warranted and honest conversations about palliative care... are often preferable.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Which specific immunohistochemical (IHC) markers guide treatment decisions for targeted therapy in breast cancer?
back:
• ER/PR receptors: Predict sensitivity to hormonal manipulation.
• HER2 receptor: Predicts response to HER2 inhibitor targeted therapy.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 165 (Book Page): [Oestrogen (ER) and progesterone (PR) receptor positivity... HER2 receptor positivity in breast or gastric cancers indicate that the tumour may respond to HER2 inhibitor targeted therapy.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Identify the primary diagnostic tumor markers for germ cell tumors and their typical associations.
back:
• Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP): Non-seminomatous germ cell tumors (80%).
• hCG: Choriocarcinoma (100%), non-seminomatous (50-80%), Seminoma (15%).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 164 (Book Page): [Alpha-fetoprotein (AFP)... Ovarian non-seminomatous germ cell tumours (80%)... Human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG)... Choriocarcinoma (100%), hydatidiform moles (97%), ovarian non-seminomatous germ cell tumours (50%–80%), seminoma (15%)]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: What are the two primary limitations of PET-CT in oncological staging?
back:
1. Not all tumor types are 'PET-avid'.
2. Low sensitivity for detecting metabolic activity in small malignant lymph nodes.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 162 (Book Page)-163: [Not all tumour types are ‘PET-avid’ and the metabolic activity of small but malignant lymph nodes may not be detected, limiting the sensitivity of PET-CT.]

category: Discuss the role of various investigations in the diagnosis and management of cancer patients
front: Q: Name the tumor marker used to screen for Medullary Cell Carcinoma of the thyroid in MEN 2 syndromes.
back: Calcitonin (produced by thyroid C cells).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 164 (Book Page): [Calcitonin 32-amino-acid peptide from C cells of thyroid. Used to screen for MEN 2: Medullary cell carcinoma of thyroid]

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: What is the earliest clinical sign of Malignant Spinal Cord Compression (MSCC)?
back: Back pain, often rapidly worsening or in a 'band' distribution, exacerbated by coughing or lying flat.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 168 (Book Page): [The earliest sign is back pain, often rapidly worsening or in a ‘band’, most marked on coughing and lying flat.]

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: Differentiate the knee and ankle reflexes in Spinal Cord vs. Cauda Equina compression.
back: Spinal Cord: Increased knee and ankle reflexes (Upper Motor Neuron). Cauda Equina: Decreased knee and ankle reflexes (Lower Motor Neuron).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 169 (Book Page): [Box 7.13: Spinal cord: Increased knee and ankle reflexes... Cauda equina: Decreased knee and ankle reflexes]

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: What is the specific glucocorticoid regimen for suspected spinal cord compression?
back: Dexamethasone 16 mg IV or oral stat, followed by 8 mg twice daily orally.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 169 (Book Page): [Box 7.14: Administer high-dose glucocorticoids: Dexamethasone 16 mg IV or oral stat; Dexamethasone 8 mg twice daily orally.]

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: What is the investigation of choice to distinguish between extra- and intravascular SVCO?
back: CT scan of the thorax.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 170 (Book Page): [The investigation of choice is a CT scan of the thorax to confirm the diagnosis and distinguish between extra- and intravascular causes.]

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: Define the neutrophil count threshold for 'neutropenic fever' in post-chemotherapy sepsis.
back: <0.5 x 10⁹/L (or <1.0 x 10⁹/L if a drop to <0.5 is anticipated within 48 hours).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 170 (Book Page): [neutropenic fever is most commonly defined as... a neutrophil count of <0.5 × 10⁹/L (or <1.0 × 10⁹/L if the nadir is anticipated to drop to < 0.5 × 10⁹/L in the next 48 hours).]

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: In neutropenic fever, which MASCC risk index score indicates high-risk status?
back: A score of less than 21 (<21).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 170 (Book Page): [Box 7.16: Score < 21 = high risk febrile neutropenia.]

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: Why must serum calcium be adjusted for albumin when diagnosing hypercalcaemia of malignancy?
back: Hypoalbuminaemia is common in cancer; total calcium values often underestimate the level of active ionised calcium.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 171 (Book Page): [It is especially important to correct for albumin in cancer because hypoalbuminaemia is common and total calcium values under-estimate the level of ionised calcium.]

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: Identify the four metabolic hallmarks of Tumour Lysis Syndrome (TLS).
back: Hyperkalaemia, hyperphosphataemia, hyperuricaemia, and hypocalcaemia.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 171 (Book Page): [Cellular destruction results in the release of potassium, phosphate, nucleic acids and purines that can cause transient hypocalcaemia, hyperphosphataemia, hyperuricaemia and hyperkalaemia.]

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: What pharmacological prophylaxis is used to prevent uric acid crystal precipitation in TLS?
back: Allopurinol (prophylaxis) or Rasburicase (recombinant urate oxidase for elevated levels).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 171 (Book Page): [Prophylaxis with allopurinol should be considered and recombinant urate oxidase (rasburicase) can be used to reduce uric acid levels when other treatments fail.]

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: What is the primary treatment for severe Immune-Related Adverse Events (IRAEs)?
back: High-dose steroids (e.g., glucocorticoids) and permanent discontinuation of the checkpoint inhibitor.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 171 (Book Page): [The focus of treatment is on dampening the immune response, often using high-dose steroids... checkpoint inhibitor immunotherapy treatment will usually be permanently discontinued.]

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: What are the three hallmark clinical features of Malignant Spinal Cord Compression (MSCC)?
back:
1. Back pain (worsened by coughing/lying flat)
2. Sensory changes in dermatomes below compression
3. Motor weakness distal to the block
4. Late-stage sphincter disturbance (urinary retention/bowel incontinence)
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 139 (Book Page): The earliest sign is back pain, often rapidly worsening or in a ‘band’... Subsequently, sensory changes develop in dermatomes below the level of compression, and motor weakness distal to the block occurs. Finally, sphincter disturbance, causing urinary retention and bowel incontinence, is observed.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: Explain the primary pathophysiology of Malignant Spinal Cord Compression (MSCC).
back: Most commonly caused by posterior extension of a vertebral body mass. It can also result from intrathecal spinal cord metastases. The thoracic region is the most frequently affected site.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 139 (Book Page): Malignant spinal cord compression often results from posterior extension of a vertebral body mass but intrathecal spinal cord metastases can cause similar signs and symptoms. The thoracic region is most commonly affected.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: What is the mandatory immediate pharmacological management for suspected MSCC?
back:
1. High-dose glucocorticoids: Dexamethasone 16 mg IV/oral stat, then 8 mg twice daily
2. Adequate analgesia
3. Urgent MRI scan of the whole spine
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 140 (Book Page): Malignant spinal cord compression is a medical emergency and should be treated with analgesia and high-dose glucocorticoid therapy (Box 7.14). [Box 7.14]: Dexamethasone 16 mg IV or oral stat; Dexamethasone 8 mg twice daily orally.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: A patient presents with facial plethora, neck vein distension, and arm oedema. Diagnosis?
back: Superior Vena Cava Obstruction (SVCO). Usually caused by extrinsic compression from lung cancer, lymphoma, or metastatic tumours, or intravascular blockage from central catheters.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 141 (Book Page): The classical presentation is with breathlessness, oedema of the arms and face, distended neck and arm veins and dusky skin coloration over the chest, arms and face. [Box 7.15]: Facial oedema (46%), Plethora of face (19%).

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: Define the clinical and laboratory criteria for Neutropenic Fever after chemotherapy.
back:
1. Temperature: Single oral ≥38.3°C OR ≥38°C sustained for >1 hour
2. Neutrophil count: <0.5 × 10^9/L (or anticipated nadir <0.5 within 48 hours)
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 141 (Book Page): Neutropenic fever is most commonly defined as a single oral temperature of ≥ 38.3°C or a temperature of ≥ 38°C sustained for over 1 hour in a patient with a neutrophil count of <0.5 × 10^9/L.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: What is the priority management step for a patient presenting with febrile neutropenia?
back: Immediate administration of high-dose empirical broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics, ideally within 1 hour of admission, before awaiting culture results.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 141 (Book Page): High-dose intravenous antibiotics should be commenced (ideally within 1 hour of admission) for all febrile patients on systemic anti-cancer therapy, without awaiting test results.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: What is the primary biochemical mechanism driving 80% of Hypercalcaemia of Malignancy cases?
back: Over-production of Parathyroid Hormone-related Protein (PTHrP). It binds to PTH receptors, stimulating osteoclastic bone resorption and increasing renal calcium reabsorption.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 142 (Book Page): It is most commonly due to over-production of PTHrP (80%), which binds to the PTH receptor and elevates serum calcium by stimulating osteoclastic bone resorption and increasing renal tubular reabsorption of calcium.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: List the clinical steps for managing severe symptomatic hypercalcaemia of malignancy.
back:
1. Aggressive IV 0.9% saline (2–4 L/day) to restore renal function
2. IV Bisphosphonates (Zoledronic acid 4 mg or Pamidronate 60–90 mg)
3. Consider Denosumab if refractory to bisphosphonates
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 142 (Book Page): Patients should initially be treated with intravenous 0.9% saline... Concurrently, intravenous bisphosphonates should be given to inhibit bone resorption. [Box 7.17]: IV 0.9% saline 2–4 L/day; Zoledronic acid 4 mg IV.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: Identify the four cardinal metabolic disturbances found in Tumour Lysis Syndrome (TLS).
back:
1. Hyperkalaemia
2. Hyperphosphataemia
3. Hyperuricaemia
4. Hypocalcaemia (secondary to phosphate binding)
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 142 (Book Page): Cellular destruction results in the release of potassium, phosphate, nucleic acids and purines that can cause transient hypocalcaemia, hyperphosphataemia, hyperuricaemia and hyperkalaemia.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: What is the cornerstone treatment for severe Immune-Related Adverse Events (IRAEs)?
back: High-dose glucocorticoids (steroids) to dampen the immune response. If severe, immunotherapy is permanently discontinued and additional immunosuppressants may be required.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 142 (Book Page): The focus of treatment is on dampening the immune response, often using high-dose steroids. Additional immunosuppressant therapies are sometimes required.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: What is the earliest clinical sign of malignant spinal cord compression?
back:
• Back pain (often worsening or 'band-like')
• Aggravated by coughing or lying flat
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 167 (Book Page): The earliest sign is back pain, often rapidly worsening or in a ‘band’, most marked on coughing and lying flat.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: What is the most common biochemical mechanism for hypercalcaemia of malignancy?
back:
• Over-production of PTHrP (80% of cases)
• Stimulates osteoclastic bone resorption and renal tubular calcium reabsorption
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 170 (Book Page): It is most commonly due to over-production of PTHrP (80%), which binds to the PTH receptor and elevates serum calcium by stimulating osteoclastic bone resorption and increasing renal tubular reabsorption of calcium.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Identify the four classic electrolyte abnormalities in Tumour Lysis Syndrome (TLS).
back:
• Hyperkalaemia
• Hyperphosphataemia
• Hyperuricaemia
• Hypocalcaemia (transient)
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 170 (Book Page): Cellular destruction results in the release of potassium, phosphate, nucleic acids and purines that can cause transient hypocalcaemia, hyperphosphataemia, hyperuricaemia and hyperkalaemia.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: A chemotherapy patient presents with fever of 38.5°C and neutrophil count 0.4 x 10^9/L. What is the immediate priority?
back:
• Empirical broad-spectrum IV antibiotics
• Administration within 1 hour of admission
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 169 (Book Page): High-dose intravenous antibiotics should be commenced (ideally within 1 hour of admission) for all febrile patients on systemic anti-cancer therapy, without awaiting test results.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: What is the standard steroid dose for suspected malignant spinal cord compression?
back:
• Dexamethasone 16 mg IV or oral (stat dose)
• Dexamethasone 8 mg twice daily orally (maintenance)
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 168 (Book Page): Dexamethasone 16 mg IV or oral stat; Dexamethasone 8 mg twice daily orally.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Define the temperature and neutrophil thresholds for 'Neutropenic Fever'.
back:
• Temp: Single oral ≥38.3°C (or ≥38°C for 1 hour)
• Neutrophils: <0.5 × 10^9/L
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 169 (Book Page): neutropenic fever is most commonly defined as a single oral temperature of ≥ 38.3°C or a temperature of ≥ 38°C sustained for over 1 hour in a patient with a neutrophil count of <0.5 × 10^9/L

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Which specific cancers are most commonly associated with malignant spinal cord compression?
back:
• Myeloma
• Prostate cancer
• Breast cancer
• Lung cancer
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 167 (Book Page): Malignant spinal cord compression... is most common in myeloma, prostate, breast and lung cancers that most frequently involve bone.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Distinguish the reflex findings in spinal cord compression versus cauda equina compression.
back:
• Spinal Cord: Increased reflexes (UMN); extensor plantar
• Cauda Equina: Decreased reflexes (LMN); flexor plantar
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 168 (Book Page): [Spinal cord] Increased (or absent) knee and ankle reflexes with extensor plantar reflex; [Cauda equina] Decreased knee and ankle reflexes with flexor plantar reflex.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: How does 0.9% saline infusion assist in managing hypercalcaemia of malignancy?
back:
• Improves renal function
• Increases urinary calcium excretion
• Corrects dehydration
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 170 (Book Page): Patients should initially be treated with intravenous 0.9% saline to improve renal function and increase urinary calcium excretion. This alone often results in clinical improvement.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies

back:
• Allopurinol (prophylaxis)

citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 170 (Book Page): Prophylaxis with allopurinol should be considered and recombinant urate oxidase (rasburicase) can be used to reduce uric acid levels when other treatments fail.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: What is the earliest clinical sign of Malignant Spinal Cord Compression (MSCC)?
back: Back pain is the earliest sign. It often worsens rapidly, presents in a 'band' distribution, and is exacerbated by coughing or lying flat.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 168 (Book Page): The earliest sign is back pain, often rapidly worsening or in a ‘band’, most marked on coughing and lying flat.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: What is the immediate pharmacological management for suspected MSCC?
back: High-dose glucocorticoids: Dexamethasone 16 mg IV or oral stat, followed by 8 mg twice daily orally.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 168 (Book Page): Malignant spinal cord compression is a medical emergency and should be treated with analgesia and high-dose glucocorticoid therapy... Dexamethasone 16 mg IV or oral stat; Dexamethasone 8 mg twice daily orally.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: Define the temperature and neutrophil thresholds for diagnosing Neutropenic Fever.
back:
- Single oral temperature: ≥ 38.3°C (or ≥ 38°C for >1 hour).
- Neutrophil count: <0.5 × 10^9/L.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 169 (Book Page): ...defined as a single oral temperature of ≥ 38.3°C or a temperature of ≥ 38°C sustained for over 1 hour in a patient with a neutrophil count of <0.5 × 10^9/L.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: What is the mandatory time window for initiating IV antibiotics in febrile neutropenia?
back: Broad-spectrum IV antibiotics should be commenced ideally within 1 hour of hospital admission.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 169 (Book Page): High-dose intravenous antibiotics should be commenced (ideally within 1 hour of admission) for all febrile patients on systemic anti-cancer therapy, without awaiting test results.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: What is the primary biochemical mechanism causing Hypercalcaemia of Malignancy (80% of cases)?
back: Over-production of PTH-related protein (PTHrP), which stimulates osteoclastic bone resorption and increases renal calcium reabsorption.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 170 (Book Page): It is most commonly due to over-production of PTHrP (80%), which binds to the PTH receptor and elevates serum calcium by stimulating osteoclastic bone resorption and increasing renal tubular reabsorption.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: Outline the first two clinical priorities in managing severe hypercalcaemia.
back:
1. IV 0.9% Saline (2–4 L/day) to restore renal function.
2. IV Bisphosphonates (e.g., Zoledronic acid 4 mg).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 170 (Book Page): Patients should initially be treated with intravenous 0.9% saline... Concurrently, intravenous bisphosphonates should be given to inhibit bone resorption.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: Which electrolyte abnormalities characterize Tumor Lysis Syndrome (TLS)?
back:
- Hyperkalaemia
- Hyperphosphataemia
- Hyperuricaemia
- Hypocalcaemia (transient)
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 170 (Book Page): Cellular destruction results in the release of potassium, phosphate, nucleic acids and purines that can cause transient hypocalcaemia, hyperphosphataemia, hyperuricaemia and hyperkalaemia.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: Differentiate the reflex findings in Spinal Cord vs. Cauda Equina compression.
back:
- Spinal Cord: Increased reflexes (UMN) with extensor plantar reflex.
- Cauda Equina: Decreased reflexes (LMN) with flexor plantar reflex.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 168 (Book Page): [Box 7.13] Spinal cord: Increased knee/ankle reflexes, extensor plantar. Cauda equina: Decreased knee/ankle reflexes, flexor plantar.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: What is the preferred investigation for confirming Superior Vena Cava Obstruction (SVCO)?
back: CT scan of the thorax (to confirm diagnosis and distinguish extra- vs. intravascular causes).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 169 (Book Page): The investigation of choice is a CT scan of the thorax to confirm the diagnosis and distinguish between extra- and intravascular causes.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: A patient on checkpoint inhibitors presents with severe colitis. What is the priority management?
back: Dampen the immune response using high-dose corticosteroids (e.g., Prednisolone or Methylprednisolone).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 170 (Book Page): The focus of treatment is on dampening the immune response, often using high-dose steroids... checkpoint inhibitor immunotherapy treatment will usually be permanently discontinued.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: What is the earliest clinical hallmark of Malignant Spinal Cord Compression (MSCC)?
back:
Back pain. Characteristics:
- Often rapidly worsening.
- Worsened by coughing or lying flat.
- Described as a 'band' or radicular pain.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 167 (Book Page): The earliest sign is back pain, often rapidly worsening or in a ‘band’, most marked on coughing and lying flat.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: What is the primary biochemical mechanism behind 80% of malignancy-associated hypercalcaemia?
back:
Over-production of PTH-related Protein (PTHrP). 
- Mechanism: Binds PTH receptors.
- Stimulates osteoclastic bone resorption.
- Increases renal tubular calcium reabsorption.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 170 (Book Page): It is most commonly due to over -production of PTHrP (80%), which binds to the PTH receptor and elevates serum calcium by stimulating osteoclastic bone resorption and increasing renal tubular reabsorption of calcium.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: Contrast the sensory loss distribution in Spinal Cord versus Conus Medullaris lesions.
back:
- Spinal Cord: Symmetrical sensory level.
- Conus Medullaris: Symmetrical saddle distribution.
- Cauda Equina: Asymmetrical radicular pattern.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 168 (Book Page): Box 7.13 Sensory loss: Spinal cord - Symmetrical, sensory level; Conus medullaris - Symmetrical, saddle distribution.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
coreConcept: Management of Malignant Spinal Cord Compression
front: Q: A cancer patient presents with back pain and leg weakness. What is the immediate stat medical management?
back:
1. Urgent MRI of whole spine.
2. Dexamethasone 16 mg IV or oral stat.
3. Adequate analgesia.
4. Neurosurgical or Oncology referral.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 168 (Book Page): Box 7.14 Management of suspected spinal cord compression: Confirm diagnosis with urgent MRI scan of whole spine; Administer high-dose glucocorticoids: Dexamethasone 16 mg IV or oral stat.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: Which drug is specifically used to rapidly lower uric acid in high-risk Tumour Lysis Syndrome (TLS)?
back:
Rasburicase (recombinant urate oxidase). 
- Converts uric acid to allantoin (more soluble).
- Used if hydration/allopurinol fail or in high-risk patients.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 170 (Book Page): Prophylaxis with allopurinol should be considered and recombinant urate oxidase (rasburicase) can be used to reduce uric acid levels when other treatments fail.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: Define the clinical temperature criteria for Neutropenic Fever in chemotherapy patients.
back:
1. Single oral temperature ≥ 38.3°C OR
2. Temperature ≥ 38°C sustained for > 1 hour
- Combined with Neutrophil count < 0.5 × 10^9/L.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 169 (Book Page): Neutropenic fever is most commonly defined as a single oral temperature of ≥ 38.3°C or a temperature of ≥ 38°C sustained for over 1 hour in a patient with a neutrophil count of <0.5 × 109/L.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: Why is CT Thorax mandatory in a patient presenting with SVCO symptoms?
back:
- Confirms diagnosis.
- Distinguishes extrinsic compression (tumor) from intravascular blockage (thrombus/central catheter).
- Identifies the primary tumor type for treatment planning.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 169 (Book Page): The investigation of choice is a CT scan of the thorax to confirm the diag - nosis and distinguish between extra- and intravascular causes.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: Contrast the electrolyte disturbances: Hypercalcaemia vs. Tumour Lysis Syndrome (TLS).
back:
- Hypercalcaemia: High Calcium, dehydration.
- TLS: Low Calcium (hypocalcaemia), High Potassium, High Phosphate, High Uric acid.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 170 (Book Page): Cellular destruction results in the release of potassium, phosphate, nucleic acids and purines that can cause transient hypocalcaemia, hyperphosphataemia, hyperuricaemia and hyperkalaemia.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: Why must total calcium be corrected for albumin in cancer patients?
back: Hypoalbuminaemia is common in cancer. Uncorrected total calcium underestimates the physiologically active 'ionised' calcium fraction.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 170 (Book Page): It is especially important to correct for albumin in can - cer because hypoalbuminaemia is common and total calcium values under -estimate the level of ionised calcium.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: Name the two most common underlying malignancies causing Superior Vena Cava Obstruction (SVCO).
back:
1. Lung Cancer.
2. Lymphoma.
- (Also metastatic tumors).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 169 (Book Page): The most common causes of extrinsic compression are lung cancer, lymphoma and metastatic tumours.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: What is the classical clinical triad of symptoms in Malignant Spinal Cord Compression (MSCC)?
back: 1. Back pain (worsened by coughing/lying flat). 2. Sensory/motor deficits (distal weakness). 3. Sphincter disturbance (urinary retention/bowel incontinence).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 167 (Book Page): [Clinical features] The earliest sign is back pain, often rapidly worsening or in a ‘band’... Subsequently, sensory changes develop... Finally, sphincter disturbance, causing urinary retention and bowel incontinence, is observed.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: What is the most common biochemical mechanism causing hypercalcaemia of malignancy?
back: Production of Parathyroid Hormone-related Protein (PTHrP) by tumour cells (80% of cases), which stimulates osteoclastic bone resorption and renal calcium reabsorption.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 170 (Book Page): It is most commonly due to over-production of PTHrP (80%), which binds to the PTH receptor and elevates serum calcium by stimulating osteoclastic bone resorption and increasing renal tubular reabsorption of calcium.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: How do reflexes differ between Spinal Cord Compression and Cauda Equina Syndrome?
back: Spinal Cord: Increased reflexes (UMN signs) and extensor plantar reflex. Cauda Equina: Decreased knee/ankle reflexes (LMN signs) and flexor plantar reflex.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 168 (Book Page): [Box 7.13] Spinal cord: Increased (or absent) knee and ankle reflexes with extensor plantar reflex. Cauda equina: Decreased knee and ankle reflexes with flexor plantar reflex.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: What is the immediate management priority for a patient with Neutropenic Fever?
back: Administration of empirical high-dose IV broad-spectrum antibiotics (e.g., Piperacillin-tazobactam) within 1 hour of admission, prior to receiving culture results.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 169 (Book Page): High-dose intravenous antibiotics should be commenced (ideally within 1 hour of admission) for all febrile patients on systemic anti-cancer therapy, without awaiting test results.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: What is the standard pharmacological intervention for suspected Malignant Spinal Cord Compression?
back: High-dose glucocorticoids: Dexamethasone 16 mg IV or oral stat, followed by 8 mg twice daily.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: In a patient with symptomatic SVCO and an unknown primary cancer, what is the critical diagnostic step?
back: Obtain a tissue biopsy. Management (Chemotherapy for sensitive tumors vs. Stenting/RT) depends entirely on identifying the specific cancer type.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 169 (Book Page): A biopsy should be obtained when the tumour type is unknown because tumour type has a major influence on treatment.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies

back: 1. Hyperkalaemia. 2. Hyperphosphataemia. 3. Hyperuricaemia. 4. Hypocalcaemia.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 170 (Book Page): Cellular destruction results in the release of potassium, phosphate, nucleic acids and purines that can cause transient hypocalcaemia, hyperphosphataemia, hyperuricaemia and hyperkalaemia.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: List the two primary steps in the medical management of severe malignant hypercalcaemia.
back: 1. Aggressive rehydration with IV 0.9% Saline (2–4 L/day). 2. IV Bisphosphonates (e.g., Zoledronic acid 4 mg) to inhibit bone resorption.

Concurrently, intravenous bisphosphonates should be given to inhibit bone resorption. [Box 7.17] IV 0.9% saline 2–4 L/day; Zoledronic acid 4 mg IV.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: What are the classic physical examination findings of Superior Vena Cava Obstruction (SVCO)?

front: Q: Why is Allopurinol or Rasburicase administered prior to treating bulky lymphomas?

front: Define neutropenic fever in oncology and state the critical timeframe for starting antibiotics.
back: - Definition: Temperature ≥38.3°C (single) or ≥38°C (sustained >1 hour) with Neutrophils <0.5 × 10^9/L. - Timing: Start broad-spectrum IV antibiotics within 1 hour of admission.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 170 (Book Page): [High-dose intravenous antibiotics should be commenced (ideally within 1 hour of admission) for all febrile patients on systemic anti-cancer therapy, without awaiting test results.]

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: List the four metabolic hallmarks of Tumour Lysis Syndrome (TLS) and its primary prophylaxis.
back: - Metabolic: Hyperkalaemia, hyperphosphataemia, hyperuricaemia, and hypocalcaemia. - Prophylaxis: Aggressive hydration and Allopurinol (or Rasburicase in high-risk cases).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 171 (Book Page): [Cellular destruction results in the release of potassium, phosphate, nucleic acids and purines that can cause transient hypocalcaemia, hyperphosphataemia, hyperuricaemia and hyperkalaemia.]

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: Which three malignancies most commonly cause malignant spinal cord compression (MSCC)?
back:
- Prostate cancer
- Breast cancer
- Lung cancer
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 167 (Book Page): Malignant spinal cord compression... is most common in myeloma, prostate, breast and lung cancers that most frequently involve bone.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: What is the most common anatomical mechanism leading to malignant spinal cord compression?
back:
- Posterior extension of a vertebral body mass into the spinal canal.
- Less commonly, intrathecal spinal cord metastases.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 167 (Book Page): Malignant spinal cord compression often results from posterior extension of a vertebral body mass but intrathecal spinal cord metastases can cause similar signs and symptoms.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: Contrast the reflexes and plantar responses in spinal cord compression versus cauda equina syndrome.
back:
- Spinal Cord: Increased knee/ankle reflexes; extensor plantar response (UMN).
- Cauda Equina: Decreased knee/ankle reflexes; flexor plantar response (LMN).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 168 (Book Page): [Box 7.13] Spinal cord: Increased knee and ankle reflexes with extensor plantar reflex. Cauda equina: Decreased knee and ankle reflexes with flexor plantar reflex.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: A cancer patient presents with new back pain and leg weakness. What is the immediate management protocol?
back:
1. Urgent MRI of the whole spine.
2. High-dose glucocorticoids (Dexamethasone 16mg stat).
3. Adequate analgesia and surgical/radiotherapy referral.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 168 (Book Page): [Box 7.14] Confirm diagnosis with urgent MRI scan of whole spine. Administer high-dose glucocorticoids: Dexamethasone 16 mg IV or oral stat... Refer for surgical decompression or urgent radiotherapy.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: What is the mandatory time-to-antibiotic window for a patient presenting with suspected neutropenic fever?
back: - High-dose IV broad-spectrum antibiotics must be commenced ideally within 1 hour of admission, before awaiting test results.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 169 (Book Page): High-dose intravenous antibiotics should be commenced (ideally within 1 hour of admission) for all febrile patients on systemic anti-cancer therapy, without awaiting test results.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: Define the temperature and neutrophil count thresholds for 'neutropenic fever'.
back:
- Temperature: Single oral ≥38.3°C (or ≥38°C sustained for >1 hour).
- Neutrophils: <0.5 × 10^9/L.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 169 (Book Page): neutropenic fever is most commonly defined as a single oral temperature of ≥ 38.3°C or a temperature of ≥ 38°C sustained for over 1 hour in a patient with a neutrophil count of <0.5 × 10^9/L.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: List four classic physical findings of Superior Vena Cava Obstruction (SVCO).
back:
1. Facial and arm oedema.
2. Distended neck/chest wall veins.
3. Elevated, non-pulsatile JVP.
4. Facial plethora or cyanosis.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 169 (Book Page): [Box 7.15] Facial swelling... Venous distension of neck... Elevated, non-pulsatile jugular venous pulse... Plethora of face.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: Differentiate the clinical signs of Conus Medullaris from Cauda Equina syndrome regarding sphincter loss.
back:
- Conus Medullaris: Early sphincter loss.
- Cauda Equina: Sphincters are often spared.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 168 (Book Page): [Box 7.13] Sphincters: Conus medullaris - Early loss; Cauda equina - Often spared.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: Explain the primary metabolic mechanism of hypercalcaemia in 80% of cancer patients.
back:
- Over-production of PTH-related Protein (PTHrP) by the tumour.
- PTHrP stimulates osteoclastic bone resorption and renal calcium reabsorption.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 170 (Book Page): It is most commonly due to over-production of PTHrP (80%), which binds to the PTH receptor and elevates serum calcium by stimulating osteoclastic bone resorption and increasing renal tubular reabsorption.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: Identify the four hallmark electrolyte abnormalities in Tumour Lysis Syndrome (TLS).
back:
1. Hyperkalaemia.
2. Hyperphosphataemia.
3. Hyperuricaemia.
4. Hypocalcaemia (transient).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 170 (Book Page): Cellular destruction results in the release of potassium, phosphate, nucleic acids and purines that can cause transient hypocalcaemia, hyperphosphataemia, hyperuricaemia and hyperkalaemia.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Define the temperature and neutrophil count criteria for neutropenic fever.
back:
• Temperature: ≥38.3°C (single) or ≥38.0°C (>1 hour).
• Neutrophil count: <0.5 × 10^9/L (or <1.0 × 10^9/L if falling).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 169 (Book Page): neutropenic fever is most commonly defined as a single oral temperature of ≥ 38.3°C or a temperature of ≥ 38°C sustained for over 1 hour in a patient with a neutrophil count of <0.5 × 10^9/L

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: What is the primary biochemical mechanism behind 80% of hypercalcaemia in malignancy?
back:
• Over-production of PTHrP (PTH-related Protein).
• Mechanism: Stimulates osteoclastic bone resorption and increases renal tubular reabsorption of calcium.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 170 (Book Page): It is most commonly due to over-production of PTHrP (80%), which binds to the PTH receptor and elevates serum calcium by stimulating osteoclastic bone resorption and increasing renal tubular reabsorption of calcium.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
coreConcept: Spinal Cord vs Cauda Equina Reflexes
front: Differentiate Malignant Spinal Cord Compression (SCC) from Cauda Equina Syndrome based on reflexes.
back:
• SCC: Symmetrical, increased knee/ankle reflexes, extensor plantars.
• Cauda Equina: Asymmetrical, decreased knee/ankle reflexes, flexor plantars.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 168 (Book Page): [Box 7.13] Spinal cord: Symmetrical... Increased (or absent) knee and ankle reflexes with extensor plantar reflex. Cauda equina: Asymmetrical... Decreased knee and ankle reflexes with flexor plantar reflex.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: A lung cancer patient presents with facial plethora and distended neck veins. What is the immediate diagnostic imaging?
back:
• CT scan of the thorax.
• Purpose: Confirms SVCO and distinguishes between extrinsic compression and intravascular thrombosis.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 169 (Book Page): The investigation of choice is a CT scan of the thorax to confirm the diagnosis and distinguish between extra- and intravascular causes.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Which pharmacological agent is used to reduce uric acid levels in high-risk Tumour Lysis Syndrome?
back:
• Rasburicase (recombinant urate oxidase).
• Use: Converts uric acid into allantoin (soluble) when hydration and allopurinol fail.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 170 (Book Page): Prophylaxis with allopurinol should be considered and recombinant urate oxidase (rasburicase) can be used to reduce uric acid levels when other treatments fail.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: List four classic physical findings associated with Superior Vena Cava Obstruction (SVCO).
back:
1. Venous distension of neck/chest wall.
2. Facial/Arm oedema.
3. Elevated non-pulsatile JVP.
4. Facial plethora/Cyanosis.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 169 (Book Page): [Box 7.15] Venous distension of neck (66%), Venous distension of chest wall (54%), Elevated, non-pulsatile jugular venous pulse (66%), Facial oedema (46%).

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: State the specific corticosteroid and dose used in the initial management of suspected Spinal Cord Compression.
back:
• Dexamethasone.
• Dose: 16mg IV or oral stat; then 8mg twice daily orally.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 168 (Book Page): [Box 7.14] Administer high-dose glucocorticoids: Dexamethasone 16 mg IV or oral stat, Dexamethasone 8 mg twice daily orally.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
coreConcept: Early Detection of Spinal Cord Compression
front: A breast cancer patient presents with new-onset back pain worsening on coughing. What is the suspected emergency?
back:
• Malignant Spinal Cord Compression (SCC).
• Note: Back pain is the earliest sign; often aggravated by coughing or lying flat.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 167 (Book Page): The earliest sign is back pain, often rapidly worsening or in a ‘band’, most marked on coughing and lying flat. [SCC] is most common in myeloma, prostate, breast and lung cancers.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Describe the electrolyte triad typically seen in Tumour Lysis Syndrome.
back:
1. Hyperkalaemia.
2. Hyperphosphataemia.
3. Hyperuricaemia.
(Secondary Hypocalcaemia also occurs).
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 170 (Book Page): Cellular destruction results in the release of potassium, phosphate, nucleic acids and purines that can cause transient hypocalcaemia, hyperphosphataemia, hyperuricaemia and hyperkalaemia.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Which four malignancies are most frequently associated with Malignant Spinal Cord Compression?
back:
1. Myeloma.
2. Prostate cancer.
3. Breast cancer.
4. Lung cancer.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 167 (Book Page): Malignant spinal cord compression... is most common in myeloma, prostate, breast and lung cancers that most frequently involve bone.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: List five high-yield oncological emergencies commonly encountered in clinical practice.
back:
1. Malignant spinal cord compression (MSCC)
2. Superior vena cava obstruction (SVCO)
3. Neutropenic fever/sepsis
4. Hypercalcaemia of malignancy
5. Tumour lysis syndrome (TLS)
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 139 (Book Page)-142: [Headings under Oncological emergencies include MSCC, SVCO, Neutropenic fever, Hypercalcaemia, and Tumour lysis syndrome].

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: What is the primary pathophysiology behind hypercalcaemia in 80% of malignancy cases?
back: Over-production of PTHrP (parathyroid hormone-related protein) which stimulates osteoclastic bone resorption and increases renal tubular reabsorption of calcium.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 142 (Book Page): It is most commonly due to over-production of PTHrP (80%), which binds to the PTH receptor and elevates serum calcium by stimulating osteoclastic bone resorption and increasing renal tubular reabsorption of calcium.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Contrast the immediate treatment of SVCO in lymphoma versus non-small cell lung cancer.
back: Lymphoma: Cytotoxic chemotherapy alone (highly chemosensitive). Non-small cell lung cancer: SVC stenting (preferred for symptom relief) or radiotherapy.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 141 (Book Page): Tumours that are exquisitely sensitive to cytotoxic chemotherapy, such as germ cell tumours and lymphoma, can be treated with cytotoxic chemotherapy alone. For most other patients with symptomatic SVCO, SVC stenting provides the best outcomes.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Q: A chemo-patient presents with a 38.5°C fever and BP 85/50. What is the immediate priority?
back: Administer broad-spectrum IV antibiotics within 1 hour and initiate aggressive fluid resuscitation for sepsis/hypotension. Do not wait for culture results.
citation: In book "Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine", Page 141 (Book Page): High-dose intravenous antibiotics should be commenced (ideally within 1 hour of admission) for all febrile patients on systemic anti-cancer therapy, without awaiting test results. Hypotension is an adverse prognostic feature.

category: Describe the common oncological emergencies
front: Specify the standard pharmacological protocol for suspected Malignant Spinal Cord Compression (MSCC).
back:
